skills.title: Uses top/bottom, on/under (upar/neeche) to say where something is
Uses inside/outside (andar/bahar) for containers
Uses near/far (paas/door) by comparing with a reference thing
Knows left/right and in-front/behind depend on which way a person faces

expectations: Says where the object is with a position word (upar, neeche, andar, bahar, paas, door)
Names the reference thing too: under the charpai, not just "under"
Near and far are always compared to something: the same thing can be near one place and far from another
Left and right belong to the person: they swap when someone faces you

misconceptions.belief: Believes left and right are fixed places in the room rather than relative to the person facing
signs: Points to the same wall as "left" for a doll that faces them
Says a friend facing them raises the right hand on the same side as their own right hand

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya stands facing you and raises her right hand. Is her hand on your right side or your left side?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya tumhare saamne khadi hai, tumhari taraf mooh karke. Woh apna right haath uthati hai. Woh tumhari right side pe hai ya left side pe?

remediation.representation: Body turn: child stands beside the doll facing the same way, raises the same hand, then walks round to face it
remediation.moveShape: Have the child physically match the other person's facing, check hands, then turn and notice the swap

misconceptions.belief: Thinks "near" or "far" is a property of the thing itself, not a comparison with something else
signs: Says "the school is far" even when asked about the shop right next to it
Uses near/far without naming what it is near to

diagnostic.prompt_en: The school is far from your home. A shop is right next to the school. Is the school near the shop or far from the shop?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: School tumhare ghar se door hai. School ke bilkul bagal mein ek dukaan hai. School us dukaan ke paas hai ya door?

options.text: Far, because the school is always far

remediation.representation: Map strip with three markers (home, shop, school); slide a finger between pairs and count steps
remediation.moveShape: Ask "near to what?" every time, then swap the reference point and ask again

misconceptions.belief: Thinks "on top of" and "inside" mean the same thing whenever the object touches the container
signs: Says the laddoo is "andar" when it sits on the lid of a closed box
Uses "mein" and "par" interchangeably for boxes and bags

diagnostic.prompt_en: A laddoo is sitting on the lid of a closed dabba. Is the laddoo inside the dabba or on top of it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek laddoo band dabbe ke dhakkan ke upar rakha hai. Laddoo dabbe ke andar hai ya upar?

remediation.representation: Two boxes side by side: one laddoo on a lid, one laddoo in an open box; lift both lids
remediation.moveShape: Contrast pair, then ask which laddoo you can see without opening the box

items.prompt_en: The cat is sitting on top of the almirah. Is the cat up or down?
items.prompt_hi: Billi almari ke upar baithi hai. Billi upar hai ya neeche?
items.answer: up, on top of the almirah
hints: Look at the almirah. Where is the cat sitting?
Is the cat on the almirah or under it?
The cat is on ___ of the almirah.
The cat is up, on top of the almirah.

items.prompt_en: The ball is in the basket. Is the ball inside or outside?
items.prompt_hi: Ball tokri mein hai. Ball andar hai ya bahar?
hints: Think about the basket. Where is the ball?
If you look into the basket, will you see the ball?
The ball is ___ the basket.
The ball is inside the basket.

items.prompt_en: Your nose, or the moon in the sky. Which one is near you?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari naak, ya aasmaan ka chaand. Tumhare paas kaun hai?
hints: Which one can you touch right now?
Can you touch the moon? Can you touch your nose?
The one I can touch is ___.
Your nose is near you; the moon is very far.

items.prompt_en: Two cats. One is on the charpai. One is under the charpai. Which cat is lower down?
items.prompt_hi: Do billiyaan hain. Ek charpai ke upar, ek charpai ke neeche. Kaun si billi neeche hai?
hints: Picture the charpai. Where is each cat?
One cat is on the charpai and one is under it. Which is closer to the floor?
The cat ___ the charpai is lower.
The cat under the charpai is lower down.

items.prompt_en: I put a laddoo on top of a closed dabba lid. Guess first: if I open the dabba, will the laddoo be inside?
items.prompt_hi: Main ek laddoo band dabbe ke dhakkan ke upar rakhti hoon. Pehle guess karo: dabba kholenge to laddoo andar milega?
items.answer: No, the laddoo is on top of the lid, not inside
hints: Where did I put the laddoo — on the lid or in the box?
The lid was closed. Could the laddoo get in?
The laddoo is ___ the lid, so it is not inside.
No — the laddoo sat on top of the lid, so the box is empty inside.

items.prompt_en: The mango is near your hand and the shop is far. How do you know the shop is far?
items.prompt_hi: Aam tumhare haath ke paas hai aur dukaan door hai. Tumhe kaise pata dukaan door hai?
items.answer: I cannot reach it from here; I have to walk a lot of steps to get there, but I can touch the mango
hints: What would you do to get the mango? And the shop?
Can you touch the shop from where you sit?
The shop is far because I have to ___ to reach it.
You can touch the mango, but you must walk many steps to reach the shop, so the shop is far.

items.prompt_en: At the station, the train is right next to Papa. The bus is across the road. Which one is near Papa?
items.prompt_hi: Station pe train Papa ke bilkul bagal mein hai. Bus sadak ke us paar hai. Papa ke paas kaun hai?
hints: Which one could Papa touch quickly?
Right next to Papa, or across the road — which is closer?
The ___ is near Papa.
The train is near Papa; the bus is farther away across the road.

items.prompt_en: Nani's village is far from your city. Nani's house is right next to the village well. Is Nani's house near the well or far from it?
items.prompt_hi: Nani ka gaon tumhare shehar se door hai. Nani ka ghar gaon ke kuen ke bilkul bagal mein hai. Nani ka ghar kuen ke paas hai ya door?
hints: We are asking about the house and the well, not your city.
Right next to means...?
Compared to the well, the house is ___.
Near — the house is far from your city but near the well. Near or far depends on what we compare with.

items.prompt_en: Make a picture in your head: a bird above a tree, and a dog under the tree. Who is lower down, the bird or the dog?
items.prompt_hi: Mann mein picture banao: ped ke upar ek chidiya, aur ped ke neeche ek kutta. Neeche kaun hai, chidiya ya kutta?
hints: Draw the tree in your head first.
The bird is above the tree. Where is the dog?
The one under the tree is the ___.
The dog is under the tree, so the dog is lower down.

items.prompt_en: First Riya stands beside you, facing the same way. Then she turns to face you. Both times she raises her right hand. When is her right hand on the same side as your right hand?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle Riya tumhare bagal mein khadi hai, same taraf dekhte hue. Phir woh ghoom kar tumhari taraf mooh karti hai. Dono baar woh right haath uthati hai. Kab uska right haath tumhare right haath ki side pe hota hai?
items.answer: When she stands beside me facing the same way
acceptable: when she faces the same way
hints: Try it: stand next to someone and both raise your right hands.
Now turn to face each other. What happened to the hands?
Facing the same way, right hands are on the ___ side.
Only when she faces the same way as you; when she faces you, her right hand is on your left side.

items.prompt_en: Bholu the bear says, "The fish is swimming outside the water bowl." Fish swim in water. What did Bholu get wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu bhaalu kehta hai, "Machhli paani ke katore ke bahar tair rahi hai." Machhli to paani mein tairti hai. Bholu ne kya galat bola?
items.answer: The fish is inside the bowl, not outside
hints: Where is the water — in the bowl or out of it?
Fish need water to swim. Where is the water?
The fish is ___ the bowl.
Bholu mixed it up: the fish swims inside the bowl, not outside.

items.prompt_en: You are playing cricket and the ball goes far, far away. Will you run a lot or a little to get it?
items.prompt_hi: Tum cricket khel rahe ho aur ball bahut door chali gayi. Laane ke liye bahut bhaagoge ya thoda?
hints: Far means it is a long way. What does that mean for your legs?
If something is far, do we need many steps or few?
Far away means I run ___.
A lot — far away means many steps to reach it.

items.prompt_en: Chintu the baby elephant does not know "near" and "far". Teach him using your school bag and the door.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu chhota haathi hai, use "paas" aur "door" nahi pata. Apne school bag aur darwaaze se use samjhao.
items.answer: Near means close, you can reach it in a step (like my bag); far means a long way, you have to walk (like the door); you always say near or far from something
hints: What will you show Chintu first, the bag or the door?
Which one can you touch without walking?
My bag is ___ because I can touch it; the door is ___ because I have to walk.
Near means close enough to touch, far means you have to walk to it — and we always say near or far from something.

items.prompt_en: Remember the cat that hid under the charpai? Was the cat on top of the charpai, or below it?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad hai woh billi jo charpai ke neeche chhupi thi? Billi charpai ke upar thi ya neeche?
hints: Think back to the hiding cat.
It was hiding — could we see it on top?
The cat was ___ the charpai.
The cat was below, under the charpai.

workedExample.problem: Where is the cat? It is under the charpai and close to the matka. Say where it is.
steps: Look at the charpai first.
Is the cat on it or below it? Below — so the cat is under the charpai.
Now look for the matka. The cat is close to it, so the cat is near the matka.
Say it all together: the cat is under the charpai, near the matka.
fadedVersion: The cat is below it, so the cat is ___ the charpai.
The cat is close to the matka, so it is ___ the matka.
Together: the cat is ___ the charpai, ___ the matka.

skills.title: Compares two objects by size: big/small, tall/short
Compares two groups by matching one-to-one: more/fewer/same
Knows spreading out or bunching up does not change how many

expectations: To compare two groups, match one from each group; the group with some left over has more
Spreading out or bunching up does not change how many there are
Big/small is about size; more/fewer is about how many
Same means nothing is left over when you match them

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the way objects are arranged (spread out or bunched up) changes how many there are; a longer row has more
signs: Points to the spread-out row as "more" without counting
Changes their answer after one row is spread, though nothing was added

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two plates each have 5 laddoos. I spread one plate's laddoos far apart. Now which plate has more?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Do plates mein 5-5 laddoo hain. Ek plate ke laddoo main door-door phaila deti hoon. Ab kis plate mein zyada hain?

remediation.representation: Match-up lines: draw a line from each laddoo to one laddoo in the other row
remediation.moveShape: Have the child pair the objects one-to-one, then push them back together and ask whether anything was added or taken away

misconceptions.belief: Judges "more" by how big the objects are, not by how many there are
signs: Says 2 watermelons are "more" than 4 grapes
Chooses the pile that looks bigger

diagnostic.prompt_en: Plate A has 2 big watermelons. Plate B has 4 small grapes. Which plate has more things?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Plate A mein 2 bade tarbooz hain. Plate B mein 4 chhote angoor. Kis plate mein zyada cheezein hain?

options.text: Plate A, the watermelons are big

remediation.representation: Replace each object with the same-sized counter, then compare the counter rows
remediation.moveShape: Separate "how big" from "how many": ask both questions about the same pair and let the answers differ

misconceptions.belief: Treats "less/fewer (kam)" as if it meant "more" and picks the bigger group
signs: Points to the bigger group when asked who has fewer
Answers "kam" and "zyada" questions the same way

diagnostic.prompt_en: Zoya has 5 bangles. Aman has 2 bangles. Who has fewer bangles?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Zoya ke paas 5 choodiyaan hain. Aman ke paas 2. Kiske paas kam choodiyaan hain?

remediation.representation: Two stacks of bangles side by side; the shorter stack is lit up for "fewer"
remediation.moveShape: Ask the "more" question first, then the "fewer" question on the same pair, so the child must give different answers

items.prompt_en: An elephant and a mouse. Which one is big?
items.prompt_hi: Haathi aur chooha. Bada kaun hai?
hints: Think of both animals standing together.
Which one could sit on a tree branch, and which one is huge?
The big one is the ___.
The elephant is big; the mouse is small.

items.prompt_en: Papa and a little baby stand side by side. Who is taller?
items.prompt_hi: Papa aur ek chhota baby saath mein khade hain. Lamba kaun hai?
hints: Picture them standing next to each other.
Whose head is higher up?
The taller one is ___.
Papa is taller; the baby is shorter.

items.prompt_en: Riya has 3 mangoes. Sonu has 1 mango. Who has more?
items.prompt_hi: Riya ke paas 3 aam hain. Sonu ke paas 1 aam. Zyada kiske paas hain?
hints: Count each person's mangoes.
Match one of Riya's mangoes with Sonu's one mango. Who has some left?
Riya has ___ left over, so she has more.
Riya has more — 3 is more than 1.

items.prompt_en: Zoya has 4 bangles. Aman has 2 bangles. Who has fewer?
items.prompt_hi: Zoya ke paas 4 choodiyaan, Aman ke paas 2. Kiske paas kam hain?
hints: Fewer means not as many. Who has not as many?
Who has more? Now — the other one has fewer.
Aman has ___ and Zoya has 4, so ___ has fewer.
Aman has fewer — 2 is less than 4.

items.prompt_en: Two rows with 4 laddoos each. I will spread one row out wide. Guess first: will it have more, fewer, or the same?
items.prompt_hi: Do line hain, dono mein 4-4 laddoo. Main ek line ko door-door phaila doongi. Pehle guess karo: zyada honge, kam, ya utne hi?
hints: Will I add any laddoo when I spread them?
Will I take any away?
Nothing added, nothing taken, so it stays ___.
The same — spreading out does not change how many; both rows still have 4.

items.prompt_en: After spreading, both rows still have the same. How can you be sure?
items.prompt_hi: Phailane ke baad bhi dono line mein barabar hain. Tum pakka kaise bata sakte ho?
items.answer: Count both rows, or match each laddoo with one in the other row and see none is left over; nothing was added or taken away
hints: What could you do with your finger to check?
Try matching one laddoo from each row.
If none are left over, the rows are ___.
Matching them one-to-one leaves none over, and no laddoo was added or taken, so they are the same.

items.prompt_en: Plate A has 2 big watermelons. Plate B has 4 small grapes. Which plate has more things?
items.prompt_hi: Plate A mein 2 bade tarbooz. Plate B mein 4 chhote angoor. Kis plate mein zyada cheezein hain?
hints: Are we asking "which is bigger" or "how many"?
Count the things on each plate.
2 watermelons and ___ grapes. More things are on plate ___.
Plate B has more things — 4 grapes is more than 2 watermelons, even though the watermelons are bigger.

items.prompt_en: 6 chappals are in a straight line. Another 6 chappals are in a heap by the door. Which has more chappals?
items.prompt_hi: 6 chappal ek seedhi line mein hain. Aur 6 chappal darwaaze ke paas dher mein. Zyada chappal kahan hain?
hints: How many chappals are in the line?
How many are in the heap?
6 and 6 are the ___.
They are the same — 6 is 6, whether in a line or a heap.

items.prompt_en: Each child gets one roti. There are 4 children and 3 rotis. Are there enough rotis?
items.prompt_hi: Har bachche ko ek roti milegi. 4 bachche hain aur 3 rotiyaan. Kya rotiyaan kaafi hain?
items.answer: No, one child gets no roti — there are fewer rotis than children
hints: Give one roti to each child in your head.
After 3 children get a roti, how many children are still waiting?
One child has ___ roti.
Not enough — one child is left without a roti, so there are fewer rotis than children.

items.prompt_en: Bholu puts 5 marbles close together and 5 marbles far apart. He says the far-apart ones are more. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu 5 kanche paas-paas rakhta hai aur 5 kanche door-door. Woh kehta hai door wale zyada hain. Kya woh sahi hai?
hints: How many marbles in each group?
Does spreading them add a marble?
Both groups have ___, so they are the same.
Bholu is wrong — both groups have 5; far apart only takes more space.

items.prompt_en: At the mela there are 5 children and 5 balloons. Each child takes one balloon. Will any balloon be left over?
items.prompt_hi: Mele mein 5 bachche hain aur 5 gubbare. Har bachcha ek gubbara leta hai. Koi gubbara bachega?
items.answer: No, none left — same number of children and balloons
hints: Give one balloon to each child, one by one.
When the fifth child takes one, how many balloons are in your hand?
Children and balloons are the ___, so ___ is left.
None is left over — 5 children and 5 balloons match exactly.

items.prompt_en: Teach Chintu: if he spreads out his laddoos on the plate, does he get more laddoos?
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko samjhao: agar woh plate pe apne laddoo phaila de, to kya laddoo zyada ho jaayenge?
items.answer: No — spreading only changes the space they take, not how many; count or match them to check
hints: What will you tell Chintu first — yes or no?
What would he have to do to really get more laddoos?
Spreading out changes the ___ but not how ___.
Spreading out does not make more — only adding laddoos does. Count or match to check.

items.prompt_en: Tenzin has 3 kites. Meenu has 5 kites. Who has more?
items.prompt_hi: Tenzin ke paas 3 patang hain. Meenu ke paas 5. Zyada kiske paas hain?
hints: Count each one's kites.
Match Tenzin's 3 with 3 of Meenu's. Who has extra?
Meenu has ___ extra.
Meenu has more — 5 is more than 3.

workedExample.problem: Plate 1 has 4 laddoos close together. Plate 2 has 4 laddoos spread out. Which plate has more?
steps: Do not look at how much space they take. Look at how many.
Match one laddoo from plate 1 with one laddoo from plate 2. Do it 4 times.
No laddoo is left over on either plate.
So both plates have the same: 4 and 4.
fadedVersion: Look at how ___, not how much space.
Match one laddoo from each plate, 4 times.

interestContexts: chappals outside a temple or gurdwara

skills.title: Sorts objects by one attribute (colour, size, shape or kind)
Says the rule used for a sort
Spots the odd one out and re-sorts the same set by a different rule
Matches things that go together in pairs

expectations: Sorting puts things that are alike in one group
You must say what is the same in each group: that is the rule
The same set can be sorted in different ways: colour, size, shape, or what it is used for
For one sort, keep the same rule all the way through

misconceptions.belief: Thinks objects can be sorted only by colour
signs: Sorts every set by colour even when asked for another rule
Says there is no other way after one colour sort

diagnostic.prompt_en: A red ball, a red block, a blue ball and a blue block. Can we sort them without using colour?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek laal ball, ek laal block, ek neeli ball aur ek neela block. Kya hum inhe rang ke bina bhi alag kar sakte hain?

options.text: Yes: balls in one group, blocks in the other

remediation.representation: Same four objects shown twice; second time all are grey so colour cannot help
remediation.moveShape: Remove the colour cue (grey them out) and ask what is still different

misconceptions.belief: Changes the rule in the middle of a sort, grouping things because they "go together" in a story rather than by one shared feature
signs: Puts a blue bat with a red ball "because bat and ball go together" during a colour sort
Groups contain mixed reasons

diagnostic.prompt_en: We are sorting by colour. The red group has a red ball and a red apple. Where does a blue bat go?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Hum rang se alag kar rahe hain. Laal group mein laal ball aur laal seb hai. Neela bat kahan jaayega?

options.text: In the red group, because bat goes with ball

remediation.representation: Rule card on top of each bin (a red splash); every item is checked against the card before dropping
remediation.moveShape: Have the child say the rule aloud before each item goes in, then check the item against it

misconceptions.belief: Believes a set has only one correct way to be sorted
signs: Says a friend who sorted by size "did it wrong" after they sorted by colour
Refuses to re-sort the same things

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya sorted buttons by colour. Sonu sorted the same buttons by size. Who is right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya ne buttons rang se alag kiye. Sonu ne wahi buttons size se alag kiye. Kaun sahi hai?

remediation.representation: Two sorting mats with the same buttons sorted two ways, side by side
remediation.moveShape: Ask for the rule of each sort; if both rules are kept the whole way, both sorts count

items.prompt_en: Spoons and plates are all mixed up. Make two groups. What are the two groups?
items.prompt_hi: Chammach aur plates mix ho gaye hain. Do group banao. Kaun se do group banenge?
items.answer: spoons in one group, plates in the other
hints: What kinds of things are in the mix?
Which things look alike?
All the ___ together, and all the ___ together.
One group of spoons and one group of plates.

items.prompt_en: Red bangles and green bangles are mixed. How will you sort them?
items.prompt_hi: Laal aur hari choodiyaan mix hain. Inhe kaise alag karoge?
items.answer: by colour: red ones together, green ones together
hints: What is different about the bangles?
Look at their colours.
All ___ bangles together, all ___ bangles together.
Sort by colour: red with red, green with green.

items.prompt_en: Group 1 has a big ball and a big box. Group 2 has a small ball and a small box. What is the rule?
items.prompt_hi: Group 1 mein badi ball aur bada dabba. Group 2 mein chhoti ball aur chhota dabba. Rule kya hai?
items.answer: by size: big things and small things
hints: What is the same inside Group 1?
Both groups have a ball and a box. So what is different?
Group 1 is ___ things, Group 2 is ___ things.
The rule is size: big things in one group, small things in the other.

items.prompt_en: Apple, banana, mango, bus. Which one does not belong?
items.prompt_hi: Seb, kela, aam, bus. Inmein se kaun alag hai?
hints: What are most of these things?
Which ones can you eat?
Three are fruits; the ___ is not.
The bus does not belong — the others are fruits.

items.prompt_en: Why does the bus not go with the apple, banana and mango?
items.prompt_hi: Bus seb, kele aur aam ke saath kyun nahi jaati?
items.answer: The others are fruits you can eat; a bus is not a fruit, it is a vehicle
hints: What is the same about apple, banana and mango?
Can you eat a bus?
They are all ___, and the bus is a ___.
The other three are fruits; the bus is a vehicle, so it does not fit the rule.

items.prompt_en: Red ball, red block, blue ball, blue block. If we sort by shape, guess how many things go in the ball group.
items.prompt_hi: Laal ball, laal block, neeli ball, neela block. Agar shape se alag karein, to guess karo ball wale group mein kitni cheezein aayengi?
hints: Forget the colours for now. Which ones are balls?
Is there a red ball? A blue ball?
The red ball and the blue ball make ___.
2 — the red ball and the blue ball go together when we sort by shape.

items.prompt_en: Rajma, chana and moong are mixed in a katori. How many groups will you make?
items.prompt_hi: Ek katori mein rajma, chana aur moong mix hain. Kitne group banaoge?
hints: How many different dals are in the katori?
Name them one by one.
Rajma, chana and moong — that is ___ groups.
3 groups, one for each dal.

items.prompt_en: Bholu is sorting by colour. In the red group he put a red apple, a red car and a yellow banana. What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu rang se alag kar raha hai. Laal group mein usne laal seb, laal gaadi aur peela kela daala. Kya galat hai?
items.answer: The yellow banana does not belong in the red group
hints: What is the rule for this group?
Check each thing: is it red?
The ___ is not red.
The yellow banana breaks the rule — it should go in a yellow group.

items.prompt_en: Draw two big circles in your head: one for fruits, one for vehicles. Where does an auto-rickshaw go?
items.prompt_hi: Mann mein do bade gole banao: ek phalon ka, ek gaadiyon ka. Auto-rickshaw kis gole mein jaayega?
hints: Is an auto-rickshaw something you eat or something you ride?
Which circle is for things we ride?
The auto goes in the ___ circle.
The vehicles circle — an auto-rickshaw is a vehicle.

items.prompt_en: Here is one chappal. What do we need to make a pair?
items.prompt_hi: Yeh ek chappal hai. Joda banane ke liye kya chahiye?
items.answer: the other chappal of the same pair
hints: How many chappals make a pair?
One is here. How many more?
We need ___ more chappal that matches.
The other matching chappal — two make a pair.

items.prompt_en: Chintu has a heap of buttons. Tell him two different ways he can sort them.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ke paas buttons ka dher hai. Use do alag tareeke batao jinse woh inhe alag kar sake.
items.answer: Any two rules, e.g. by colour and by size (also shape or number of holes); keep one rule for each sort
hints: What can be different about buttons?
Think about colour. What else — size? holes?
Way 1: by ___. Way 2: by ___.
He can sort by colour or by size (or shape, or holes) — both are fine if he keeps the same rule.

items.prompt_en: After washing, the family's clothes are in one big pile. How could you sort them so everyone gets theirs?
items.prompt_hi: Dhulne ke baad ghar ke saare kapde ek dher mein hain. Kaise alag karoge taaki sabko apne kapde mil jaayein?
items.answer: Sort by whose clothes they are — one pile for each person
hints: What do we want at the end — everyone gets what?
What rule would make one pile for Papa, one for Mummy...?
Sort by ___ the clothes belong to.
Sort by person — one pile for each family member.

items.prompt_en: Pencils and crayons are mixed in a box. What two groups can you make?
items.prompt_hi: Ek dabbe mein pencil aur crayon mix hain. Kaun se do group bana sakte ho?
hints: What two kinds of things are in the box?
Which ones are alike?
All ___ together and all ___ together.
Pencils in one group, crayons in the other.

items.prompt_en: Riya sorted the buttons by colour. Sonu sorted the same buttons by size. Who is right?
items.prompt_hi: Riya ne buttons rang se alag kiye. Sonu ne wahi buttons size se. Kaun sahi hai?
hints: Did Riya keep one rule?
Did Sonu keep one rule?
If each kept one rule, then ___ are right.
Both are right — the same things can be sorted in more than one way.

workedExample.problem: Sort these: red ball, blue ball, red block, blue block. Say your rule.
steps: Choose one rule. Let us choose shape.
Pick up the red ball. It is a ball — it goes in the ball group.
Pick up the red block. It is a block — it goes in the block group.
Do the same for the blue ball and the blue block.
Say the rule: balls in one group, blocks in the other — sorted by shape.
fadedVersion: The red ball is a ___, so it goes in the ball group.
The red block goes in the ___ group.
Do the same for the blue ball and the blue block.

skills.title: Identifies long things around them
Identifies round things around them
Knows turning or moving a thing does not change its shape

expectations: Long things stretch out a lot in one direction (pencil, sugarcane, rope)
Round things curve all the way around with no corners (bangle, roti, wheel)
Turning, flipping or moving a thing does not change its shape
Some things have a long part and a round part (a bottle)

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a shape changes its name when it is turned or moved
signs: Says a long stick standing up is now "short"
Says a bangle hung on a nail is "not round any more"

diagnostic.prompt_en: A long stick is lying on the floor. I stand it up. Does it become short?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek lambi lakdi zameen pe padi hai. Main use khada kar deti hoon. Kya woh chhoti ho gayi?

options.text: No, it is still the same long stick

remediation.representation: Animated object rotates slowly with a ghost outline of the start position overlaid
remediation.moveShape: Mark both ends, turn the object back and forth, and ask whether the ends moved closer together

misconceptions.belief: Thinks only one typical thing (like a ball) is round; a bangle, coin or wheel does not count
signs: Says a bangle is not round because it has a hole
Only names balls when asked for round things

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is a bangle round, even though it has a hole in the middle?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya choodi gol hai, jabki uske beech mein chhed hai?

options.text: Yes, it curves all the way around
No, it has a hole so it is not round

remediation.representation: Finger-trace: trace the edge of a bangle, a coin, a roti and a wheel; none has a corner
remediation.moveShape: Collect many different round things and ask what is the same about all of them

misconceptions.belief: Uses "long" to mean big or heavy
signs: Calls a watermelon "long" because it is big
Picks the bulkiest object as the longest

diagnostic.prompt_en: A watermelon is big. A pencil is thin. Which one is long?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tarbooz bada hai. Pencil patli hai. Lamba kaun hai?

options.text: The watermelon, because it is big

remediation.representation: Stretch test: hold each object end to end with arms; long things need arms stretched far apart in one direction
remediation.moveShape: Ask "big?" and "long?" separately about the same object so the answers can differ

items.prompt_en: Sugarcane or a laddoo — which one is long?
items.prompt_hi: Ganna ya laddoo — lamba kaun hai?
hints: Picture both in your hand.
Which one stretches out far?
The long one is the ___.
Sugarcane is long; a laddoo is round.

items.prompt_en: A roti or a book — which one is round?
items.prompt_hi: Roti ya kitaab — gol kaun hai?
hints: Trace each edge in the air with your finger.
Which one has corners?
The one with no corners is the ___.
The roti is round; a book has corners.

items.prompt_en: Name one round thing in your kitchen.
items.prompt_hi: Apni rasoi ki ek gol cheez ka naam batao.
items.answer: Any round thing, e.g. roti, plate, tawa, katori rim, onion
hints: Think of what Mummy or Papa cooks on, or eats from.
What do we cook rotis on? What shape is it?
A round thing in my kitchen is a ___.
A roti, a thali or a tawa — all are round.

items.prompt_en: A watermelon is big. A pencil is thin. Which one is long?
items.prompt_hi: Tarbooz bada hai. Pencil patli hai. Lamba kaun hai?
hints: Big and long are not the same word.
Which one stretches out far in one direction?
The ___ is long, the watermelon is round.
The pencil is long — the watermelon is big but round.

items.prompt_en: A long pencil is lying down. I stand it up. Guess first: is it still long?
items.prompt_hi: Ek lambi pencil leti hui hai. Main use khada kar deti hoon. Pehle guess karo: kya ab bhi lambi hai?
hints: Did I cut the pencil?
Are the two ends still the same distance apart?
Turning it does not change its ___.
Yes — it is the same pencil, still long, just standing up.

items.prompt_en: Why do we call a bangle round?
items.prompt_hi: Choodi ko gol kyun kehte hain?
items.answer: It curves all the way around and has no corners
hints: Trace a bangle with your finger.
Did your finger hit any corner?
It goes all the way ___ with no ___.
A bangle curves all the way around with no corners, so it is round.

items.prompt_en: The wheels of an auto-rickshaw — are they long or round?
items.prompt_hi: Auto-rickshaw ke pahiye — lambe hain ya gol?
hints: Picture an auto wheel turning.
Does a wheel have any corners?
Wheels are ___.
Round — wheels curve all around so they can turn.

items.prompt_en: Bholu hung a bangle on a nail instead of keeping it on the table. He says it is not round any more. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu ne choodi table pe rakhne ke bajaye keel pe taang di. Woh kehta hai ab choodi gol nahi rahi. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No, it is still round — moving it does not change its shape
hints: Did the bangle bend or break?
Trace it again on the nail. Any corners now?
Moving it does not change its ___.
Bholu is wrong — the bangle is still round wherever it hangs.

items.prompt_en: Draw a roti in the air with your finger. Did you make a straight line or a circle?
items.prompt_hi: Ungli se hawa mein roti banao. Seedhi line bani ya gola?
hints: Start at one point and go around.
Did your finger come back to where it started?
A roti is a ___.
A circle — a roti is round.

items.prompt_en: Why are bicycle wheels round and not long like a stick?
items.prompt_hi: Cycle ke pahiye gol kyun hote hain, lakdi jaise lambe kyun nahi?
items.answer: Round wheels can roll smoothly; a long stick cannot roll along the road
hints: What does a wheel have to do when the cycle moves?
Can a stick roll along like a wheel?
Round things can ___.
Round wheels roll smoothly, so the cycle can move.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to find one long thing and one round thing in the room.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao kamre mein ek lambi aur ek gol cheez kaise dhoondhe.
items.answer: Long: it stretches far in one direction (like a broom or rope). Round: trace the edge — it curves all around with no corners (like a plate or clock)
hints: How will Chintu know something is long?
How will he check if something is round?
Long things ___ far; round things have no ___.
Long things stretch far one way; round things curve all around with no corners.

items.prompt_en: Is a one-rupee coin round or long?
items.prompt_hi: Ek rupaye ka sikka gol hai ya lamba?
hints: Picture the coin in your palm.
Trace its edge — any corners?
The coin is ___.
Round — a coin curves all the way around.

items.prompt_en: A water bottle: is it long, round, or both?
items.prompt_hi: Paani ki bottle: lambi hai, gol hai, ya dono?
items.answer: both: it is long, and it is round when you look at its top or bottom
hints: Look at the bottle from the side. What do you see?
Now look at it from the top. What shape is the cap?
From the side it is ___, from the top it is ___.
Both — the bottle is long, and its top and bottom are round.

workedExample.problem: Is a bangle long or round?
steps: Hold the bangle and trace its edge with a finger.
Your finger goes all the way around and comes back to the start.
There are no corners anywhere.
So the bangle is round.
fadedVersion: Trace the edge with a finger.
The finger goes all the way ___ and comes back.

skills.title: Predicts that things with a curved surface roll
Predicts that things with flat faces slide
Predicts that things with flat tops and bottoms stack
Knows the same thing can roll one way and stand or stack another way

expectations: Things with a curved surface roll
Things with flat faces slide and do not roll
Flat tops and bottoms let things stack
The same object can roll on its side and stand or stack on its flat end (bottle, tin)
Shape decides rolling, not how big or heavy something is

misconceptions.belief: Believes only balls can roll
signs: Says a bottle or a tin cannot roll
Names only balls when asked what rolls

diagnostic.prompt_en: Can a water bottle roll?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya paani ki bottle lurhak sakti hai?

options.text: Yes, when it lies on its side

remediation.representation: Live test: lay a bottle on a slanting notebook and let go
remediation.moveShape: Predict, then test with a real household object, then ask which part of the bottle touched the slope

misconceptions.belief: Thinks whether something rolls depends on how big or heavy it is, not its shape
signs: Says a big drum will not roll because it is heavy
Says a small box will roll because it is light

diagnostic.prompt_en: A big heavy drum is lying on its side. A small matchbox is next to it. Both are on a slope. Which one will roll?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek bada bhaari drum karvat leta hai. Uske paas ek chhoti maachis ki dibbi. Dono dhalaan pe hain. Kaun lurhkega?

options.text: The matchbox, because it is small and light

remediation.representation: Pair of objects with the same size but different shapes, then same shape but different sizes
remediation.moveShape: Hold one feature fixed and vary the other, asking each time whether it rolled

misconceptions.belief: Thinks anything with a round part can never be stacked
signs: Says ghee tins or glasses cannot be stacked
Tries to stack tins on their sides and gives up

diagnostic.prompt_en: Can you stack tins of ghee one on top of another?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya ghee ke dibbe ek ke upar ek rakh sakte hain?

options.text: Yes, standing on their flat tops and bottoms
No, they are round so they will roll

remediation.representation: Tin shown two ways: lying on its side (rolls) and standing on its end (stacks)
remediation.moveShape: Turn the same object so a different face touches the floor and ask again

items.prompt_en: A ball and a book are on a slope. Which one rolls down?
items.prompt_hi: Ek ball aur ek kitaab dhalaan pe hain. Kaun lurhak ke neeche aayega?
hints: Which one is round all over?
Which one has flat sides?
The ___ rolls.
The ball rolls; the book slides or stays.

items.prompt_en: Can you make a tower with matchboxes?
items.prompt_hi: Kya maachis ki dibbiyon se tower bana sakte ho?
items.answer: Yes, they have flat sides so they stack
hints: Think about the sides of a matchbox.
Are they flat or curved?
Flat sides can ___.
Yes — matchboxes have flat sides, so they stack into a tower.

items.prompt_en: A matchbox is on a slanting notebook. Will it roll or slide?
items.prompt_hi: Maachis ki dibbi tedhi copy pe rakhi hai. Woh lurhkegi ya phisalegi?
hints: Which part of the matchbox touches the notebook?
Is that part flat or curved?
Flat faces ___.
It slides — a flat face does not roll.

items.prompt_en: I lay a water bottle on its side on a slope. Guess first: will it roll?
items.prompt_hi: Main paani ki bottle ko karvat se dhalaan pe rakhti hoon. Pehle guess karo: lurhkegi?
hints: Which part of the bottle touches the slope now?
Is that part curved?
A curved side can ___.
Yes — on its side, the curved part touches the slope, so it rolls.

items.prompt_en: The ball rolled and the book did not. Why?
items.prompt_hi: Ball lurhak gayi aur kitaab nahi. Kyun?
items.answer: The ball is curved all over; the book has flat sides and corners
hints: What shape is the ball? What shape is the book?
Does the book have corners?
The ball is ___ and the book is ___.
The ball is curved all over so it rolls; the book has flat sides, so it does not.

items.prompt_en: A steel glass standing up, and the same glass lying on its side. Which one will roll?
items.prompt_hi: Ek steel ka glass khada hai, aur wahi glass karvat leta hai. Kaun sa lurhkega?
items.answer: the glass lying on its side
hints: Which part touches the floor in each case?
Standing up, the flat bottom touches. Lying down?
The one lying on its ___ rolls.
The glass on its side rolls; standing up, its flat bottom keeps it still.

items.prompt_en: Which will roll: a laddoo or a piece of barfi?
items.prompt_hi: Kaun lurhkega: laddoo ya barfi ka tukda?
hints: What shape is a laddoo?
What shape is barfi — does it have flat sides?
The round one is the ___.
The laddoo rolls because it is round; barfi has flat sides.

items.prompt_en: A big heavy drum on its side and a small matchbox, both on a slope. Guess which one rolls.
items.prompt_hi: Ek bada bhaari drum karvat se aur ek chhoti maachis ki dibbi, dono dhalaan pe. Guess karo kaun lurhkega.
hints: Forget big and small. Look at the shapes.
Which one has a curved side touching the slope?
The ___ has a curved side.
The drum rolls — its curved side touches the slope. Size does not decide.

items.prompt_en: Bholu says ghee tins cannot be stacked because they are round. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu kehta hai ghee ke dibbe upar-neeche nahi rakh sakte kyunki woh gol hain. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No — standing up, their flat tops and bottoms let them stack
hints: What does the top of a ghee tin look like?
Is the bottom flat too?
Flat tops and bottoms can ___.
Bholu is wrong — tins stand on flat ends and stack well.

items.prompt_en: Show with your hand how a ball goes down a slope. Now show how a box goes down. How are they different?
items.prompt_hi: Haath se dikhao ball dhalaan se kaise neeche aati hai. Ab dikhao dabba kaise aata hai. Fark kya hai?
items.answer: The ball turns over and over as it rolls; the box slides down flat without turning
hints: Move your hand like the ball. Is it turning?
Now the box. Is it turning, or moving flat?
The ball ___, the box ___.
The ball rolls by turning; the box slides flat.

items.prompt_en: Why do auto-rickshaws have round wheels and not square ones?
items.prompt_hi: Auto-rickshaw ke pahiye gol kyun hote hain, chaukor kyun nahi?
items.answer: Round wheels roll smoothly; square ones have corners and would bump and not roll
hints: What would happen at the corners of a square wheel?
Which shape keeps rolling smoothly?
Round wheels ___ smoothly.
Round wheels roll smoothly; corners on square wheels would bump and stop.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to know if something will roll, slide or stack.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao kaise pata kare koi cheez lurhkegi, phisalegi ya ek ke upar ek rakhi jaayegi.
items.answer: Look at the part touching the floor: curved rolls, flat slides; flat top and bottom stacks; turning it can change what it does
hints: What part of the object should Chintu look at?
Curved part touching? Flat part touching?
Curved ___, flat ___, flat top and bottom ___.
Curved surfaces roll, flat faces slide, flat tops and bottoms stack — and turning it can change which.

items.prompt_en: Will an orange roll or slide?
items.prompt_hi: Santra lurhkega ya phisalega?
hints: What shape is an orange?
Is it curved all over?
Curved things ___.
It rolls — an orange is round all over.

workedExample.problem: Will a tin of ghee roll, slide or stack?
steps: Look at the tin lying on its side: the curved part touches the floor, so it rolls.
Look at the tin standing up: the flat bottom touches the floor, so it stays.
Its top is flat too, so another tin can sit on it — it stacks.
So the tin rolls on its side and stacks when standing up.
fadedVersion: Lying on its side, the ___ part touches the floor, so it rolls.
Standing up, the ___ bottom touches the floor.
The top is flat, so it can ___.
The tin rolls on its ___ and stacks when standing up.

skills.title: Says number words 1 to 9 in the same order every time
Touches or points to each object exactly once while counting
Knows the last number said tells how many in all
Counts out a given number from a bigger group

expectations: Say the numbers in the same order every time: 1, 2, 3...
Touch each thing once — do not skip and do not count anything twice
The last number you say tells how many there are in all
Counting from a different end gives the same total

misconceptions.belief: Counts some objects twice or skips some (one-to-one correspondence error)
signs: Says number words faster or slower than pointing
Touches one mango twice and gets one extra

diagnostic.prompt_en: When we count mangoes, can we touch the same mango two times?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Jab hum aam ginte hain, kya ek hi aam ko do baar chhoo sakte hain?

remediation.representation: Move-aside counting: slide each counted mango into a "done" basket
remediation.moveShape: Have the child move each object as it is counted so nothing can be touched twice

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the last number said is just the name of the last object, not how many there are
signs: Recounts from 1 when asked "how many?"
Points to the last object when asked how many there are

diagnostic.prompt_en: We counted: 1, 2, 3, 4 mangoes. How many mangoes are there?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Humne gina: 1, 2, 3, 4 aam. Kitne aam hain?

remediation.representation: After counting, all objects are circled together with the last number written on the circle
remediation.moveShape: After each count, sweep a hand over the whole group and say the total once

misconceptions.belief: Thinks counting in a different order or from the other end will give a different number
signs: Insists on recounting after the objects are re-ordered
Gives a new guess when asked to count from the other end

diagnostic.prompt_en: We counted 6 rotis from left to right. If we count them from right to left, how many will there be?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Humne 6 rotiyaan baayen se daayen gini. Agar daayen se baayen ginein, to kitni hongi?

remediation.representation: Count the same row twice in different colours, ending on the same number
remediation.moveShape: Ask for a prediction before the second count, then count to check

items.prompt_en: Count with me from 1. What comes after 4?
items.prompt_hi: Mere saath 1 se gino. 4 ke baad kya aata hai?
hints: Start at 1 and say the numbers.
5 comes after 4.

items.prompt_en: 1 mango, 2 mangoes, 3 mangoes. How many mangoes in all?
items.prompt_hi: 1 aam, 2 aam, 3 aam. Kul kitne aam?
hints: Listen to the last number we said.
We stopped at which number?
The last number was ___.
3 — the last number tells how many.

items.prompt_en: Count the fingers on one of your hands. How many?
items.prompt_hi: Apne ek haath ki ungliyaan gino. Kitni hain?
hints: Touch each finger once.
Start with your thumb: 1...
5 fingers on one hand.

items.prompt_en: There are lots of rotis. Give 4 rotis to Dadi. When do you stop counting?
items.prompt_hi: Bahut saari rotiyaan hain. Dadi ko 4 rotiyaan do. Ginna kab rokoge?
hints: How many does Dadi want?
Count as you give: 1, 2...
I stop when I say ___.
Stop at 4 — that is how many Dadi wants.

items.prompt_en: You counted 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 parrots. Why is the answer 5?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne gina 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 tote. Jawaab 5 kyun hai?
items.answer: The last number I said tells how many parrots there are in all
hints: Which number did you say last?
Does that number tell about one parrot or all of them?
The ___ number I say tells how many.
The last number counted, 5, tells how many parrots there are altogether.

items.prompt_en: We counted 6 chairs starting from the door. If we start from the window side, guess how many we will get.
items.prompt_hi: Humne darwaaze se shuru karke 6 kursiyaan gini. Agar khidki ki taraf se shuru karein, to guess karo kitni aayengi?
hints: Did any chair move or go away?
Only the starting side changed.
Same chairs, so the count is ___.
6 — starting from the other end does not change how many.

items.prompt_en: Bholu counts 4 mangoes but touches one mango two times. He says 5. What went wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu 4 aam ginta hai par ek aam ko do baar chhoo leta hai. Woh kehta hai 5. Kya galat hua?
items.answer: He counted one mango twice — there are 4
hints: How many times should we touch each mango?
Bholu touched one mango how many times?
One mango got counted ___, so the real count is ___.
He touched one mango twice; touching each once gives 4.

items.prompt_en: Riya touched each of 3 balls once and said 3. Sonu skipped one ball and said 2. Who counted right?
items.prompt_hi: Riya ne 3 balls mein se har ek ko ek baar chhua aur kaha 3. Sonu ne ek ball chhod di aur kaha 2. Kisne sahi gina?
hints: What is the rule for touching when we count?
Who touched every ball?
The one who touched each ball ___ is right.
Riya — she touched each ball once and got 3.

items.prompt_en: Count my claps: clap, clap, clap, clap. How many claps?
items.prompt_hi: Meri taaliyaan gino: taali, taali, taali, taali. Kitni taaliyaan?
hints: Count one number for each clap.
Clap... 1. Clap... 2...
4 claps — sounds can be counted too.

items.prompt_en: Show 6 with your fingers. How did you make it?
items.prompt_hi: Ungliyon se 6 dikhao. Kaise banaya?
items.answer: 5 fingers on one hand and 1 more on the other
hints: One hand has how many fingers?
You need one more than a full hand.
A full hand, 5, and ___ more.
A full hand (5) and 1 more finger make 6.

items.prompt_en: 4 cousins are coming over. Each one gets 1 mango. How many mangoes should you take out of the basket?
items.prompt_hi: 4 cousins aa rahe hain. Har ek ko 1 aam milega. Tokri se kitne aam nikaaloge?
hints: One mango for each cousin. How many cousins?
Take one mango for each cousin as you count.
One for each of ___ cousins.
4 mangoes — one for each cousin.

items.prompt_en: Teach Chintu how to count the bananas on a plate.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao plate ke kele kaise gine.
items.answer: Touch each banana once, say the numbers in order, do not skip or count twice; the last number tells how many
hints: What does Chintu do with his trunk for each banana?
Can he touch one banana two times?
Touch each ___, and the ___ number is how many.
Touch each banana once while saying 1, 2, 3...; the last number is the total.

items.prompt_en: 1 kite, 2 kites, 3 kites, 4 kites, 5 kites, 6 kites. How many kites?
items.prompt_hi: 1 patang, 2 patang, 3, 4, 5, 6 patang. Kitni patang?
hints: Which number did we stop at?
The last number tells...
The last number was ___.
6 kites — the last number tells how many.

workedExample.problem: How many mangoes are in the basket? (There are 5.)
steps: Take one mango out and say "1". Put it on the side.
Take the next mango and say "2". Put it with the first.
Keep going: 3, 4, 5. The basket is empty.
The last number was 5, so there are 5 mangoes.
fadedVersion: Take one mango out and say "___".
Keep going: 3, 4, ___. The basket is empty.
The last number was ___, so there are ___ mangoes.

skills.title: Matches a numeral to a group of that many
Matches number names (one/ek) to numerals
Writes and reads numerals the right way round (6 vs 9, 2 vs 5)
Knows zero is the number for none

expectations: Each numeral stands for how many things
The number name (five, paanch) and the numeral 5 mean the same amount
Direction matters: 6 turned upside down is 9, a different number
Zero means none, and zero is a number too; it comes just before 1

misconceptions.belief: Writes 6 and 9 or 2 and 5 mirror-wise and thinks it does not matter
signs: Writes 6 upside down and says it is still six
Reads a 9 as 6 on a bus or house number

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya says if you turn a 6 upside down, it is still six. Is she right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya kehti hai 6 ko ulta kar do to bhi woh chhah hi rahega. Kya woh sahi hai?

remediation.representation: Numeral cards with the matching dot group printed under each; flip the card and the dots change
remediation.moveShape: Flip the card, recount the dots under it, and let the child notice the amount changed

misconceptions.belief: Believes zero means nothing is there so it is not a number
signs: Says "no number" or stays silent when all objects are gone
Leaves zero out when counting back

diagnostic.prompt_en: The plate had 2 rotis. Both were eaten. How many rotis are on the plate now?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Plate mein 2 rotiyaan thi. Dono kha li gayi. Ab plate pe kitni rotiyaan hain?

options.text: Zero — 0 is the number for none
There is no number, nothing is there

remediation.representation: Empty ten-frame with the numeral 0 shown beside it; counting back on a number line that starts at 0
remediation.moveShape: Take objects away one at a time, saying each number, until the last step lands on zero

misconceptions.belief: Thinks 0 comes after 9 (as on a phone keypad), not before 1
signs: Counts "7, 8, 9, 0"
Places 0 at the end when ordering numerals

diagnostic.prompt_en: When we count backwards: 3, 2, 1, ___. What comes next?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ulta ginte hain: 3, 2, 1, ___. Aage kya aayega?

remediation.representation: Number line starting at 0 next to a phone keypad; point out the keypad is a button layout, not counting order
remediation.moveShape: Count down to zero with objects being removed, then place 0 at the start of the number line

items.prompt_en: Clap, clap, clap, clap. Which number is that?
items.prompt_hi: Taali, taali, taali, taali. Yeh kaun sa number hua?
hints: Count the claps one by one.
Clap 1, clap 2...
4 claps — the number is 4.

items.prompt_en: Which number is called "seven"? Say it in Hindi too.
items.prompt_hi: "Seven" kaun sa number hai? Hindi mein bhi bolo.
hints: Count up from 1 in English till you say "seven".
... five, six, seven.
Seven is ___, and in Hindi it is ___.
Seven is 7, and in Hindi it is saat.

items.prompt_en: There were 2 rotis. You ate both. How many rotis are left?
items.prompt_hi: 2 rotiyaan thi. Tumne dono kha li. Kitni bachi?
hints: You ate both. Is any roti left on the plate?
What number do we say when there is none?
None left means ___.
0 — zero rotis are left.

items.prompt_en: Why do we need the number zero?
items.prompt_hi: Humein zero number ki zaroorat kyun hai?
items.answer: To say there is none of something — like an empty plate
hints: Think about an empty plate. How many rotis?
What number tells us "none"?
Zero tells us there are ___.
Zero tells us there are none — it is the number for empty.

items.prompt_en: 6 and 9 look a bit alike. How are they different?
items.prompt_hi: 6 aur 9 thode ek jaise dikhte hain. Inmein fark kya hai?
items.answer: 6 has its circle at the bottom, 9 has its circle at the top; 9 is three more than 6
hints: Write both in the air.
Where is the round part in 6? In 9?
In 6 the circle is at the ___; in 9 it is at the ___.
6 has the circle at the bottom, 9 at the top — they are different numbers.

items.prompt_en: Bholu wrote his house number, 6, upside down. He says it is still six. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu ne apna ghar ka number 6 ulta likh diya. Woh kehta hai yeh ab bhi chhah hai. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No — an upside-down 6 looks like 9, a different number
hints: Turn a 6 upside down in your head.
Which number does it look like now?
Upside-down 6 looks like ___.
Bholu is wrong — upside down it reads 9, so the postman would go to the wrong house.

items.prompt_en: 3 birds sit on a wire. All 3 fly away. Guess what number is left on the wire.
items.prompt_hi: Taar pe 3 chidiya baithi hain. Teeno udd jaati hain. Guess karo taar pe kitni bachi?
hints: All of them flew away.
Is any bird still sitting?
None left is the number ___.
0 — no birds are left.

items.prompt_en: I say the number name "eight". Show me 8 with your fingers.
items.prompt_hi: Main bolti hoon "eight". Ungliyon se 8 dikhao.
items.answer: A full hand (5) and 3 more fingers
hints: One hand gives you how many?
How many more after a full hand to reach 8?
5 and ___ make 8.
5 fingers on one hand and 3 on the other make 8.

items.prompt_en: Your house number is 7. How many claps will you clap for it?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare ghar ka number 7 hai. Uske liye kitni taaliyaan bajaoge?
hints: The number tells how many claps.
What is the house number?
I clap ___ times.
7 claps for the number 7.

items.prompt_en: In cricket, a batter got out without scoring a single run. What is his score?
items.prompt_hi: Cricket mein ek batsman bina ek bhi run banaye out ho gaya. Uska score kya hai?
hints: How many runs did he make?
Not even one. What number is that?
His score is ___.
His score is 0 — zero runs.

items.prompt_en: What number is "nau"?
items.prompt_hi: "Nau" kaun sa number hai?
hints: Count in Hindi: ek, do, teen...
... saat, aath, nau.
Nau is ___.
Nau is 9 — nine.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu what zero means, using rotis on a plate.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko roti aur plate se samjhao ki zero ka matlab kya hai.
items.answer: If the plate is empty — all rotis eaten — there are zero rotis; zero is the number for none
hints: Start with a few rotis on the plate. Then what happens?
When all are eaten, what is on the plate?
An empty plate has ___ rotis.
When every roti is eaten, the plate has zero rotis — zero means none.

items.prompt_en: Count backwards: 3, 2, 1, ___. What comes next?
items.prompt_hi: Ulta gino: 3, 2, 1, ___. Aage kya aayega?
hints: Each step we take one away.
One less than 1 is...?
0 comes just before 1.

workedExample.problem: Which numeral shows this many: 3 birds, then all of them fly away?
steps: Start with 3 birds: the numeral is 3.

fadedVersion: Start with 3 birds: the numeral is ___.
The last one flies away: the numeral is ___.

Finds one more and one less than a number
Compares groups by how many, not by object size

In order the numbers go 1, 2, 3 up to 9

misconceptions.belief: Thinks bigger-looking objects make a bigger number
signs: Says 4 big mangoes are more than 7 small ones
Picks the pile that looks bigger

remediation.representation: Number line with a "one less" arrow pointing back and a "one more" arrow pointing forward
remediation.moveShape: Act it out: hold 5 counters, take one away, recount

items.prompt_en: 5 or 2 — which number is more?
items.prompt_hi: 5 ya 2 — kaun sa number zyada hai?
hints: Which one do you reach later when counting?
We reach ___ later, so it is more.
5 is more than 2.

items.prompt_en: 3 or 6 — which number is less?
items.prompt_hi: 3 ya 6 — kaun sa number kam hai?
hints: Which comes first when counting?
The one that comes first is ___.
3 is less than 6.

items.prompt_en: What is one more than 4?
items.prompt_hi: 4 se ek zyada kitna?

After 4 comes...
One more than 4 is 5.

items.prompt_en: What is one less than 7?
items.prompt_hi: 7 se ek kam kitna?
hints: One less means one step back.
What comes just before 7?
One less than 7 is 6.

items.prompt_en: 7 small mangoes or 4 big mangoes — which has more mangoes?
items.prompt_hi: 7 chhote aam ya 4 bade aam — kismein zyada aam hain?
hints: Are we asking how big, or how many?
Count each group.
7 and 4: ___ is more.
7 small mangoes — 7 is more than 4, whatever their size.

items.prompt_en: Why do 7 small mangoes count as more than 4 big ones?
items.prompt_hi: 7 chhote aam 4 bade aam se zyada kyun maane jaate hain?
items.answer: We count how many, not how big; 7 comes after 4 so it is more
hints: What does "more mangoes" ask about — size or number?
Which number comes later, 4 or 7?
We count how ___, and 7 is ___ than 4.
Because "more" is about how many: 7 is more than 4.

items.prompt_en: Put these in order, smallest first: 5, 2, 8.
items.prompt_hi: Inhe chhote se bade ke order mein lagao: 5, 2, 8.
hints: Which one comes first when counting?
Find the smallest, then the next.

items.prompt_en: There are 5 mangoes. I will add one more. Guess how many there will be.
items.prompt_hi: 5 aam hain. Main ek aur daaloongi. Guess karo kitne ho jaayenge?
hints: One more means the next number.
What comes after 5?
6 — one more than 5.

items.prompt_en: Bholu put numbers in order: 1, 2, 3, 5, 4, 6. Which ones are mixed up?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu ne numbers order mein lagaye: 1, 2, 3, 5, 4, 6. Kaun se ulte ho gaye?
items.answer: 5 and 4 are swapped; it should be 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
hints: Count 1 to 6 and check each place.
After 3, what should come?
After 3 comes ___, then ___.
4 and 5 are swapped: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

items.prompt_en: Tenzin has 3 big footballs. Meenu has 5 small marbles. Who has more things?
items.prompt_hi: Tenzin ke paas 3 badi footballs hain. Meenu ke paas 5 chhote kanche. Zyada cheezein kiske paas hain?
hints: Forget the size. How many does each have?
3 or 5 — which is more?
___ is more than 3.
Meenu — 5 is more than 3.

items.prompt_en: Walk forward on a number line: 1, 2, 3... Which do you reach later, 3 or 7? So which is more?
items.prompt_hi: Number line pe aage chalo: 1, 2, 3... Pehle 3 aayega ya 7? To zyada kaun hai?
hints: Start at 1 and step forward.
Do you reach 3 or 7 first?
We reach ___ later, so it is more.
7 is further along, so 7 is more than 3.

items.prompt_en: You have ₹5. A toffee packet costs ₹8. Is your money enough?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare paas ₹5 hain. Toffee ka packet ₹8 ka hai. Kya paise kaafi hain?
hints: Which is more, 5 or 8?
Is what you have more or less than the price?
5 is ___ than 8.
Not enough — ₹5 is less than ₹8.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to find who has more: 4 big laddoos or 6 small laddoos.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao kaise pata kare kiske paas zyada hain: 4 bade laddoo ya 6 chhote laddoo.
items.answer: Count each group; size does not matter; 6 comes after 4 so 6 small laddoos are more
hints: What should Chintu do first — look at size or count?
Which number is more, 4 or 6?
Count, ignore ___, and ___ is more.
Count both: 6 is more than 4, so the 6 small laddoos are more — size does not matter.

items.prompt_en: What comes just before 9?
items.prompt_hi: 9 se theek pehle kya aata hai?
hints: Count up to 9 slowly.
8 comes just before 9.

workedExample.problem: Who has more: Riya with 7 small mangoes or Sonu with 4 big mangoes?
steps: The question is "how many", so ignore how big the mangoes are.
Count Riya's mangoes: 7.

When counting, 7 comes after 4, so 7 is more. Riya has more.

skills.title: Finds the partner that makes 10 with a given number
Lists many different pairs that make 10
Knows a pair in either order makes the same 10 (3 and 7, 7 and 3)

expectations: 10 can be split into two parts in many ways: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5
If one part gets 1 bigger, the other part gets 1 smaller, and the whole stays 10
3 and 7 makes the same 10 as 7 and 3
The two parts together always make the whole

misconceptions.belief: Believes there is only one way to make 10 (like 5 and 5)
signs: Gives only 5 and 5 when asked for ways to make 10
Says 6 and 4 "is not ten"

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is 5 and 5 the only way to make 10?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya 10 banane ka sirf ek hi tareeka hai — 5 aur 5?

options.text: No — 6 and 4, 7 and 3 and more also make 10

remediation.representation: Ten-bead string with a slider: move the divider one bead at a time and read both parts
remediation.moveShape: Shift one bead across at a time and ask for the new pair, building the full list together

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a pair in the other order (7 and 3 vs 3 and 7) is a different fact that must be counted again
signs: Recounts 7 and 3 right after solving 3 and 7
Says 7 and 3 might be a different number

diagnostic.prompt_en: 3 and 7 make 10. What do 7 and 3 make?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 3 aur 7 milkar 10 bante hain. 7 aur 3 milkar kitne bante hain?

options.text: I have to count again — it may be different

remediation.representation: Turn the ten-frame around: the same beads, viewed from the other side
remediation.moveShape: Physically rotate the bead string 180 degrees and ask whether any bead was added

misconceptions.belief: Does not see the part-whole trade-off: thinks when one part grows the other part stays the same or also grows
signs: Says 7 and 4 make 10 after learning 6 and 4
Changes one part without adjusting the other

diagnostic.prompt_en: 6 and 4 make 10. If the first part becomes 7, what must the other part be to still make 10?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 6 aur 4 se 10 banta hai. Agar pehla hissa 7 ho jaaye, to 10 banane ke liye doosra hissa kitna hona chahiye?

remediation.representation: Ten-frame with two colours: move one counter from blue to red and watch blue shrink
remediation.moveShape: Move exactly one counter across and ask what happened to each part

items.prompt_en: Show 10 fingers. Fold 3 fingers down. How many are still up?
items.prompt_hi: 10 ungliyaan dikhao. 3 ungliyaan mod lo. Kitni khadi hain?
hints: Fold them slowly and look.
Count the fingers still standing.
3 folded, so ___ are up.
7 fingers are still up — 3 and 7 make 10.

items.prompt_en: 8 and how many more make 10?
items.prompt_hi: 8 mein kitne aur milaayein to 10 banega?
hints: Start at 8 and count up to 10.
8... 9, 10. How many steps?
8 and ___ make 10.
8 and 2 make 10.

items.prompt_en: 4 and how many more make 10?
items.prompt_hi: 4 mein kitne aur milaayein to 10 banega?
hints: Show 4 fingers. How many are down?
Count the folded fingers.
4 and ___ make 10.
4 and 6 make 10.

items.prompt_en: Tell me two different ways to make 10.
items.prompt_hi: 10 banane ke do alag tareeke batao.
items.answer: Any two of: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5
hints: Use your fingers. Fold some — what pair do you see?
Fold a different number. What pair now?
One way is ___ and ___; another is ___ and ___.
For example 3 and 7, and 4 and 6 — there are many ways.

items.prompt_en: 3 and 7 make 10. Guess without counting: 7 and 3 make how many?
items.prompt_hi: 3 aur 7 se 10 banta hai. Bina gine guess karo: 7 aur 3 se kitna banega?
hints: Are they the same numbers?
Only the order changed.
Same numbers, so the same ___.
10 — swapping the order does not change the total.

items.prompt_en: Why do 7 and 3 make the same as 3 and 7?
items.prompt_hi: 7 aur 3, 3 aur 7 jitna hi kyun banta hai?
items.answer: They are the same things, just swapped around — nothing was added or taken away
hints: Did we add any bead?
Did we take any bead away?
We only changed the ___.
They are the same beads in a different order, so the total stays 10.

items.prompt_en: Riya made 10 with 5 and 5. Sonu made 10 with 9 and 1. Who is right?
items.prompt_hi: Riya ne 5 aur 5 se 10 banaya. Sonu ne 9 aur 1 se. Kaun sahi hai?
hints: Check Riya: 5 and 5 is...?
Check Sonu: 9 and 1 is...?
Both make ___.
Both are right — 10 can be made in many ways.

items.prompt_en: Bholu says 6 and 3 make 10. Check with your fingers. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu kehta hai 6 aur 3 se 10 banta hai. Ungliyon se check karo. Kya woh sahi hai?
hints: Show 6 fingers, then 3 more.
Count all the fingers up.
6 and 3 make ___, so we need ___ with 6.
Bholu is wrong — 6 and 3 make 9; 6 and 4 make 10.

items.prompt_en: A ten-frame has 10 boxes. 7 boxes have beads. How many boxes are empty?
items.prompt_hi: Ten-frame mein 10 khaane hain. 7 khaanon mein moti hain. Kitne khaane khaali hain?
hints: How many boxes in all?
7 are full. Count on from 7 to 10.
7 and ___ make 10.
3 boxes are empty — 7 and 3 make 10.

items.prompt_en: 6 and 4 make 10. Now the first part is 7. Guess: what should the other part be?
items.prompt_hi: 6 aur 4 se 10 banta hai. Ab pehla hissa 7 hai. Guess karo: doosra hissa kitna hona chahiye?
hints: The first part got bigger by 1.
To keep 10, what must happen to the other part?
One part goes up by 1, the other goes ___ by 1: 4 becomes ___.
3 — 7 and 3 make 10.

items.prompt_en: On a string of 10 beads, 4 are red and the rest are blue. How many are blue?
items.prompt_hi: 10 motiyon ki maala mein 4 laal hain, baaki neele. Kitne neele hain?
hints: How many beads in all?
Count on from 4 up to 10.
4 and ___ make 10.
6 blue beads — 4 and 6 make 10.

items.prompt_en: A box had 10 laddoos. Didi ate some and 4 are left. How many did she eat?
items.prompt_hi: Dabbe mein 10 laddoo the. Didi ne kuch kha liye aur 4 bache. Didi ne kitne khaaye?
hints: 10 is the whole. 4 is one part.
What goes with 4 to make 10?
4 and ___ make 10.
She ate 6 — 6 and 4 make 10.

items.prompt_en: Teach Chintu how to find all the ways to put 10 bananas into two baskets.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao 10 kele do tokriyon mein kitne tareekon se rakh sakte hain.
items.answer: Start with 1 in one basket and 9 in the other, then move one banana at a time: 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5; the total stays 10
hints: What is a first way Chintu could try?
If he moves one banana across, what happens to each basket?
One basket goes ___, the other goes ___, total stays ___.
Move one banana at a time: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5 — always 10.

items.prompt_en: Quick one: 9 and how many make 10?
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi batao: 9 aur kitne se 10 banta hai?
hints: 9 is just before 10.
How many steps from 9 to 10?
9 and ___ make 10.
9 and 1 make 10.

diagnostic.prompt_en: A bundle of 10 sticks and 3 loose sticks. How many sticks in all?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 10 teeliyon ka ek bandal aur 3 khuli teeliyaan. Kul kitni teeliyaan?

remediation.representation: Ten-frame filled (shows the 10 inside) next to loose counters
remediation.moveShape: Count on from 10: "ten... eleven, twelve, thirteen" while touching the loose sticks

items.prompt_en: One bundle of 10 sticks and 2 loose sticks. How many sticks?
items.prompt_hi: 10 teeliyon ka ek bandal aur 2 khuli teeliyaan. Kitni teeliyaan?
hints: How many sticks are in the bundle?
Start at 10 and count the loose ones.
12 sticks — 10 and 2 more.

items.prompt_en: 17 is 1 ten and how many ones?
items.prompt_hi: 17 mein 1 das aur kitni ekaai?
hints: Look at the second digit of 17.
10 and how many more make 17?
17 is 1 ten and ___ ones.
7 ones — 10 and 7 make 17.

items.prompt_en: Write sixteen in numbers. Which digit comes first?
items.prompt_hi: Sixteen (solah) ko number mein likho. Pehle kaun sa digit aata hai?
hints: Sixteen is one ten and six ones.
Which goes on the left, the ten or the ones?
The ten goes first: 1, then ___.
16 — the 1 (one ten) comes first, then 6.

items.prompt_en: For fourteen, Riya writes 14 and Sonu writes 41. Who is right?
items.prompt_hi: Fourteen ke liye Riya likhti hai 14 aur Sonu likhta hai 41. Kaun sahi hai?
hints: Fourteen is one ten and four ones.
Which digit shows the ten, and where does it go?
The ten goes first, so it is ___.
Riya — 14. 41 would be forty-one, a much bigger number.

items.prompt_en: In 15, the 1 looks small. Why does it mean 10 sticks?
items.prompt_hi: 15 mein 1 chhota sa dikhta hai. Woh 10 teeliyon ka matlab kyun hai?
items.answer: It is in the tens place — it stands for one bundle of ten
hints: Build 15 with a bundle and loose sticks.
Which digit tells about the bundle?
The 1 is in the ___ place, so it means one ___.
The 1 is in the tens place, so it means one bundle of ten sticks.

items.prompt_en: One bundle of 10 and 3 loose sticks. Guess how many sticks altogether before we count.
items.prompt_hi: 10 ka ek bandal aur 3 khuli teeliyaan. Ginne se pehle guess karo kul kitni teeliyaan?
hints: How many sticks hide inside the bundle?
Start at 10 and add the loose ones.
13 — the bundle is 10, and 3 more make 13.

items.prompt_en: An egg tray holds 10 eggs and it is full. 4 more eggs are in a bowl. How many eggs?
items.prompt_hi: Ande ki tray mein 10 ande aate hain aur woh bhari hai. 4 ande katori mein bhi hain. Kul kitne ande?
hints: The full tray is how many?
Count on from 10 with the bowl eggs.
10 and 4 make ___.
14 eggs — one ten and four ones.

items.prompt_en: Show 18 using one full ten-frame and some extra counters. How many extra counters?
items.prompt_hi: 18 ko ek bhare ten-frame aur kuch extra counters se dikhao. Kitne extra counters?
hints: A full ten-frame is how many?
10 and how many more make 18?
10 and ___ make 18.
8 extra counters — 10 and 8 make 18.

items.prompt_en: Bholu says 19 means 1 stick and 9 sticks, so 10 sticks in all. What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu kehta hai 19 matlab 1 teeli aur 9 teeli, yaani kul 10 teeliyaan. Kya galat hai?

hints: Look at the 1 in 19. Which place is it in?
How many sticks does one ten mean?
The 1 means ___ sticks, so 10 and 9 is ___.
Bholu forgot the 1 is a ten: 19 is 10 and 9, which is 19 sticks.

items.prompt_en: Which is more: 13 or 18?
items.prompt_hi: Kaun zyada hai: 13 ya 18?
hints: Both have one ten.

8 ones is more than ___ ones.
18 — both have one ten, and 8 ones is more than 3.

items.prompt_en: 20 is how many tens?
items.prompt_hi: 20 mein kitne das hain?
hints: Count bundles of 10: one bundle is 10.
How many bundles make 20?
10 and 10 make 20, so ___ tens.
20 is 2 tens and no loose ones.

items.prompt_en: Papa brought a box of 10 laddoos and 6 loose laddoos. How many laddoos in all?

hints: The box is one ten.
Count on from 10 with the loose laddoos.

16 laddoos — one ten and six ones.

The 1 is one ___, the 3 is three ___.
1 is one ten, 3 is three ones: 10 and 3 make 13.

items.prompt_en: 1 ten and 1 one make which number?
