skills.title: Solves putting-together stories within 9
Counts on from the larger number
Reads and writes a + b = c and knows = means "is the same as"
Knows the order of the numbers does not change the sum

expectations: Adding means putting groups together to find how many in all
Start from the bigger number and count on the rest
The = sign means both sides are the same amount; the answer can be on either side
Changing the order of the numbers does not change the total

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the = sign means "write the answer here" rather than "is the same as"
signs: Says 5 = 2 + 3 is "backwards" or wrong
Writes 5 in the blank of 4 + ___ = 5 + 1 (adds everything)

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is this true: 5 = 2 + 3?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya yeh sahi hai: 5 = 2 + 3?

options.text: Yes — both sides are the same amount, 5
No — the answer has to come after the = sign

remediation.representation: Pan balance: 5 cubes on one pan, 2 and 3 cubes on the other; = means the pans are level
remediation.moveShape: Show equations written both ways and check each with the balance

misconceptions.belief: Always counts all from 1 instead of counting on from the larger number
signs: Counts 1 to 6 again before adding 2 more
Puts out fingers for both numbers every time

diagnostic.prompt_en: A box has 6 laddoos and you add 2 more. Where should you start counting?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Dabbe mein 6 laddoo hain aur tum 2 aur daalte ho. Ginna kahan se shuru karoge?

options.text: Start at 1 and count all of them

remediation.representation: Covered cup: the 6 are hidden under a cup labelled 6; only the 2 extras are visible
remediation.moveShape: Hide the first group so it cannot be recounted and say its number, then count on

misconceptions.belief: When counting on, counts the starting number again as "one" and gets one less
signs: For 5 + 3 says "5, 6, 7" and answers 7
Off-by-one answers that are always one short

diagnostic.prompt_en: For 5 + 3, Bholu counts "5, 6, 7" and says 7. Is he right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 5 + 3 ke liye Bholu ginta hai "5, 6, 7" aur kehta hai 7. Kya woh sahi hai?

remediation.representation: Number-line hops: each hop lands on a new number; count the hops, not the starting spot
remediation.moveShape: Have the child put a finger up for each new number said, so the start number gets no finger

items.prompt_en: 3 parrots are on a guava tree. 2 more come. How many parrots now?
items.prompt_hi: Amrood ke ped pe 3 tote hain. 2 aur aa gaye. Ab kitne tote?
hints: How many were there first?
Start at 3 and count the 2 new ones.
5 parrots — 3 and 2 more make 5.

items.prompt_en: 2 and 2 more make how many?
items.prompt_hi: 2 aur 2 milkar kitne?
hints: Show 2 fingers on each hand.
Count all the fingers up.
2 and 2 make 4.

items.prompt_en: Start at 6 and count on 2 more. Where do you land?
items.prompt_hi: 6 se shuru karo aur 2 aage gino. Kahan pahunche?
hints: Say 6 in your head. Now count 2 new numbers.
The first new number after 6 is 7.
8 — counting on 2 from 6 gives 7, 8.

items.prompt_en: 4 + 3 = ___. What goes in the blank?
items.prompt_hi: 4 + 3 = ___. Khaali jagah mein kya aayega?
hints: Start at the bigger number, 4.
Count on 3: 5...

items.prompt_en: 2 + 5 is 7. Guess 5 + 2 without counting.
items.prompt_hi: 2 + 5 = 7 hota hai. Bina gine guess karo 5 + 2 kitna?
hints: Are these the same two numbers?
Only the order changed.
Same numbers, same ___.
7 — swapping the order does not change the sum.

items.prompt_en: For 7 + 2, why can we start at 7 instead of starting at 1?
items.prompt_hi: 7 + 2 ke liye hum 1 se nahi, 7 se kyun shuru kar sakte hain?
items.answer: The 7 is already counted, so we only need to count the 2 more: 8, 9
hints: What do we already know about the first group?
If we count 1 to 7, which number do we end on?
We know there are ___, so we just count ___ more.
We already know there are 7, so we count on just 2: 8, 9.

items.prompt_en: Which one is true: 5 = 2 + 3, or 5 = 2 + 2?
items.prompt_hi: Kaun sa sahi hai: 5 = 2 + 3, ya 5 = 2 + 2?
hints: = means both sides are the same amount.
Work out each right side: 2 + 3 and 2 + 2.
5 = 2 + 3 is true, because 2 + 3 is also 5.

items.prompt_en: Bholu does 5 + 3 by counting "5, 6, 7" and says 7. What went wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu 5 + 3 karta hai, ginta hai "5, 6, 7" aur kehta hai 7. Kya galat hua?
items.answer: He counted the 5 again; start after 5: 6, 7, 8 — the answer is 8
hints: How many numbers should he say after 5?
Did "5" count as one of the 3?
Start after 5: 6, 7, ___.
He counted the 5 again — the 3 new numbers are 6, 7, 8, so 8.

items.prompt_en: 3 people are sitting in an auto-rickshaw. 1 more gets in. How many people?
items.prompt_hi: Auto-rickshaw mein 3 log baithe hain. 1 aur baith gaya. Kitne log?
hints: How many were there first?
One more joins. What is one more than 3?
4 people.

items.prompt_en: Make up a short story for 4 + 4 = 8.
items.prompt_hi: 4 + 4 = 8 ke liye ek chhoti si kahani banao.
items.answer: Any story where 4 things join 4 more to make 8 (e.g., 4 birds on a wire, 4 more come, now 8)
hints: Pick something you like — birds, cars, rotis.
First there are 4. What happens next?
There were 4 ___, then 4 more came, now there are ___.
For example: 4 kites in the sky, 4 more fly up, now there are 8 kites.

items.prompt_en: In cricket you hit a 4, then you run 3 more runs. What is your score?
items.prompt_hi: Cricket mein tumne ek chauka maara, phir 3 run aur bhaage. Tumhara score kya hai?
hints: A four gives you how many runs?
Then 3 more runs. Count on from 4.
7 runs.

items.prompt_en: 6 = 4 + ___. What number is missing?
items.prompt_hi: 6 = 4 + ___. Kaun sa number chhoot gaya?
hints: = means both sides must be the same amount.
4 and how many more make 6?
4... 5, 6 — that is ___ more.
2, because 4 + 2 is the same as 6.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to find 3 + 4 using fingers.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao ungliyon se 3 + 4 kaise nikaale.
items.answer: Start with the bigger number 4 in your head, put up 3 fingers and count on: 5, 6, 7 — the answer is 7
hints: Which number should Chintu start with?
How many fingers does he put up for counting on?
Start at ___, count on ___: 5, 6, 7.
Start at 4, count on 3 fingers: 5, 6, 7 — so 3 + 4 = 7.

items.prompt_en: 1 mango and 5 more mangoes. How many mangoes?
items.prompt_hi: 1 aam aur 5 aam aur. Kitne aam?
hints: Start with the bigger number.
Start at 5 and count on 1.
6 mangoes.

workedExample.problem: 6 laddoos are in a box. 3 more are added. How many laddoos?
steps: Say the bigger number: 6. It is already counted.
Count on 3 more, one finger for each new number: 7, 8, 9.
The last number is 9.
Write it: 6 + 3 = 9.

skills.title: Solves taking-away stories within 9
Solves "how many more" comparing stories
Counts back on a number line
Knows subtraction order matters and links it to addition

expectations: Taking away means some go away; we find how many are left
Start with the whole and take away a part
"How many more" means compare two groups and find the extra
5 − 3 is not the same as 3 − 5: you cannot take 5 away from 3 things
If 2 + 3 = 5, then 5 − 3 = 2: subtraction undoes adding

misconceptions.belief: Believes subtraction can be done in any order, like 3 − 5 = 2
signs: Writes 3 − 5 = 2
Always takes the smaller number from the bigger one, whatever the order

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is 3 − 5 the same as 5 − 3?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya 3 − 5 aur 5 − 3 ek hi baat hai?

options.text: No — 5 − 3 is 2, but you cannot take 5 away from 3 things

remediation.representation: Real objects: hold 3 toffees and try to give away 5
remediation.moveShape: Act out both orders with real objects so the impossible one is felt

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a "how many more" question means adding the two numbers
signs: Says 8 for "Riya has 5, Zoya has 3, how many more does Riya have?"
Hears "more" and adds

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya has 5 bangles. Zoya has 3. How many more does Riya have?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya ke paas 5 choodiyaan hain. Zoya ke paas 3. Riya ke paas kitni zyada hain?

remediation.representation: Two rows matched one-to-one; the unmatched bangles are lit up
remediation.moveShape: Line up the two groups, match pairs, and count only the leftovers

misconceptions.belief: When counting back, counts the starting number as the first step and gets one too many
signs: For 8 − 3 says "8, 7, 6" and answers 6
Answers that are always one more than correct

diagnostic.prompt_en: For 8 − 3, Bholu counts back "8, 7, 6" and says 6. Is he right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 8 − 3 ke liye Bholu ulta ginta hai "8, 7, 6" aur kehta hai 6. Kya woh sahi hai?

options.text: No — the 3 steps back are 7, 6, 5, so 5

remediation.representation: Number-line hops backwards; each hop lands on a new number
remediation.moveShape: Fold one finger down for each new number said while counting back

items.prompt_en: 5 rotis are on the plate. Bhaiya eats 2. How many rotis are left?
items.prompt_hi: Plate pe 5 rotiyaan hain. Bhaiya 2 kha leta hai. Kitni bachi?
hints: Start with 5. Take 2 away.
Fold 2 fingers from 5. How many are up?
5 take away 2 is ___.
3 rotis are left.

items.prompt_en: You have 4 balloons. 1 pops. How many are left?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare paas 4 gubbare hain. 1 phoot gaya. Kitne bache?
hints: One less than 4 is...?
Count back one step from 4.
4 take away 1 is ___.
3 balloons are left.

items.prompt_en: Start at 7. Count back 3. Where are you now?
items.prompt_hi: 7 se shuru karo. 3 peeche gino. Ab kahan ho?
hints: Say 7 in your head. Now 3 new numbers going back.
The first number back from 7 is 6.
4 — counting back 3 from 7 gives 6, 5, 4.

items.prompt_en: Riya has 5 bangles. Zoya has 3 bangles. How many more does Riya have?
items.prompt_hi: Riya ke paas 5 choodiyaan hain. Zoya ke paas 3. Riya ke paas kitni zyada hain?
hints: Match each of Zoya's bangles with one of Riya's.
How many of Riya's have no partner?
5 and 3: Riya has ___ extra.
2 more — after matching 3 pairs, Riya has 2 left over.

items.prompt_en: 6 birds sit on a wire. If all 6 fly away, guess how many stay.
items.prompt_hi: Taar pe 6 chidiya baithi hain. Agar saari 6 udd jaayein, to guess karo kitni bachengi?
hints: All of them fly away.
Is any bird left?
6 take away 6 is ___.
0 — none stay.

items.prompt_en: 2 + 3 = 5. So what is 5 − 3? How do you know without counting?
items.prompt_hi: 2 + 3 = 5. To 5 − 3 kitna? Bina gine kaise pata?
items.answer: 2, because 2 and 3 make 5, so taking the 3 away leaves 2
hints: 5 is made of which two parts?
If you take one part away, what is left?
2 and 3 make 5, so 5 − 3 is ___.
2 — 5 is 2 and 3; take the 3 away and 2 is left.

items.prompt_en: 5 − 3 and 3 − 5: which one can you do with 5 toffees in your hand?
items.prompt_hi: 5 − 3 aur 3 − 5: haath mein 5 toffee ho to kaun sa kar sakte ho?
hints: You start with 5. Can you give away 3?
If you had only 3, could you give away 5?
With 5 toffees I can do ___.
5 − 3 = 2; 3 − 5 would need 5 toffees from only 3.

items.prompt_en: Bholu says 3 − 5 = 2, just like 5 − 3. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu kehta hai 3 − 5 = 2, bilkul 5 − 3 jaisa. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No — the order matters; you cannot take 5 away from 3 things
hints: Try it: hold 3 toffees. Give away 5.
Can you do it?
In subtraction the ___ matters.
Bholu is wrong — 5 − 3 = 2, but 3 − 5 cannot be done with 3 toffees.

items.prompt_en: 9 children are on the school bus. 4 get off at the first stop. How many are still on the bus?
items.prompt_hi: School bus mein 9 bachche hain. Pehle stop pe 4 utar gaye. Bus mein kitne bache?
hints: Start with 9. Take away 4.
Count back 4 from 9.
5 children are still on the bus.

items.prompt_en: Show 8 − 3 on a number line: start at 8 and jump back 3. Where do you land?
items.prompt_hi: 8 − 3 ko number line pe dikhao: 8 se shuru karo aur 3 jump peeche. Kahan pahunche?
hints: Put your finger on 8.
Jump back one at a time: first jump lands on 7.
You land on 5.

items.prompt_en: Your team needs 7 runs to win. You have scored 4. How many more runs do you need?
items.prompt_hi: Team ko jeetne ke liye 7 run chahiye. Tumne 4 bana liye. Aur kitne run chahiye?
hints: Start at 4 and count up to 7.
4... 5, 6, 7. How many steps?
4 and ___ more make 7.
3 more runs.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to find how many bananas are left when 2 of his 6 bananas are eaten.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao, uske 6 kelon mein se 2 kha liye jaayein to kitne bachenge, yeh kaise nikaale.
items.answer: Start with 6, take away 2 (count back 5, 4), and 4 are left
hints: What number does Chintu start with?
Then what happens to 2 bananas?
Start at 6, take away ___, count back: 5, ___.
Start with 6, take away 2 by counting back 5, 4 — 4 are left.

items.prompt_en: 4 mangoes. You eat 1. How many are left?
items.prompt_hi: 4 aam hain. Tumne 1 kha liya. Kitne bache?
hints: One less than 4?
Count back one step.
4 take away 1 is ___.
3 mangoes.

workedExample.problem: 7 kites are flying. 2 get cut in a kite fight. How many are still flying?
steps: Start with all the kites: 7.
Take away 2. Count back two steps, folding a finger for each: 6, 5.
You land on 5.
Write it: 7 − 2 = 5. 5 kites are still flying.

skills.title: Fills up to 10 first by splitting the second number
Knows 10 and some ones make a teen number
Starts from the bigger number and keeps the total the same when splitting

expectations: Find how many more the bigger number needs to make 10
Break the other number into that part and the rest
10 and the rest make a teen number
The number you split gets smaller by what you gave away; the total stays the same

misconceptions.belief: Thinks adding always means counting every object from 1
signs: Counts 1 to 13 for 8 + 5
Does not use a full ten-frame as 10

diagnostic.prompt_en: For 8 + 5, which is a faster way?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 8 + 5 ke liye kaun sa tareeka jaldi hai?

remediation.representation: Ten-frame crate: fill the crate first, then read the full crate as 10 without counting
remediation.moveShape: Cover the full ten-frame and ask how many are under the cover

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the number you borrowed from stays the same after giving part of it to make 10
signs: For 8 + 5 says 10 + 5 = 15
Moves counters but reads the second group unchanged

diagnostic.prompt_en: For 8 + 5, you give 2 from the 5 to make 10. How many are left in the 5-group?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 8 + 5 mein 5 wale group se 2 dekar 10 banaya. 5 wale group mein ab kitne bache?

remediation.representation: Two ten-frames: counters physically slide from the second frame to the first
remediation.moveShape: After moving, count what is left in the second frame before adding

misconceptions.belief: Writes 10 and 3 as 103 (joins the numbers side by side)
signs: Writes 103 for 10 + 3
Says "ten-three"

diagnostic.prompt_en: 10 and 3 more make which number?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 10 aur 3 aur milkar kaun sa number?

remediation.representation: Place-value cards: the 3 card slides on top of the 0 in 10
remediation.moveShape: Overlay the ones card on the zero of the ten card to show 13

items.prompt_hi: 10 + 4 kitna?
hints: 10 is one ten. Add 4 ones.
Count on from 10: 11...
14 — one ten and four ones.

items.prompt_en: 9 + 3: give 1 from the 3 to the 9. What do you get?
items.prompt_hi: 9 + 3: 3 mein se 1, 9 ko de do. Kya mila?
hints: 9 needs how many to make 10?
After giving 1, how many are left from the 3?
10 and ___ make ___.

items.prompt_en: 8 tomatoes and 5 tomatoes. Fill the 10-crate first. How many in all?
items.prompt_hi: 8 tamatar aur 5 tamatar. Pehle 10 ka crate bharo. Kul kitne?
hints: How many more does 8 need to fill the crate?
Move 2 from the 5. How many are left?
Full crate 10 and ___ left: ___.
13 — 8 + 2 fills the crate, 3 are left, 10 + 3 = 13.

items.prompt_hi: 7 + 6 kitna?
hints: 7 needs how many to make 10?
Take 3 from the 6. What is left?
10 and ___ make ___.
7 + 3 = 10, and 3 left from the 6: 10 + 3 = 13.

items.prompt_en: 9 + 4. If we move 1 from the 4 to the 9, guess what is left in the 4-group.
items.prompt_hi: 9 + 4. Agar 4 mein se 1, 9 ki taraf le jaayein, to guess karo 4 wale group mein kitne bachenge?
hints: The 4-group gave one away.
One less than 4 is...?
4 take away 1 is ___.
3 are left — so 9 + 4 becomes 10 + 3 = 13.

items.prompt_en: Why do we make 10 first when adding 8 + 5?
items.prompt_hi: 8 + 5 jodte waqt pehle 10 kyun banaate hain?
items.answer: 10 and a few more is easy — it is just a teen number, so we do not have to count every one
hints: What is 10 + 3? Was that hard?
Is 8 + 5 harder to see at once?
Making 10 turns it into 10 + ___, which is easy.
Because 10 plus some ones is quick to read as a teen number — no counting all.

items.prompt_en: Bholu does 8 + 5: he moves 2 to make 10, then says 10 + 5 = 15. What went wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu 8 + 5 karta hai: 2 le jaakar 10 banata hai, phir kehta hai 10 + 5 = 15. Kya galat hua?
items.answer: After giving 2 away, the 5 became 3, so it is 10 + 3 = 13
hints: Where did the 2 come from?
After giving 2, how many are left from the 5?
The 5 became ___, so 10 + ___ = 13.
He forgot the 5 gave away 2 — it is 10 + 3 = 13.

items.prompt_en: 10 + 6 and 6 + 10 — same or different?
items.prompt_hi: 10 + 6 aur 6 + 10 — ek jaise ya alag?
hints: Are they the same two numbers?
Work out 10 + 6.
Both are ___.
Same — order does not matter; both are 16.

items.prompt_en: A train has 9 coaches. 5 more coaches are joined. How many coaches now?
items.prompt_hi: Ek train mein 9 dibbe hain. 5 aur dibbe jode gaye. Ab kitne dibbe?
hints: 9 needs how many to make 10?
Take 1 from the 5. What is left?
10 and ___ make ___.
14 coaches — 9 + 1 = 10, then 4 more.

items.prompt_en: Two ten-frames: one has 8 counters, one has 6. Move counters to fill the first frame. How many are left in the second, and what is the total?
items.prompt_hi: Do ten-frame: ek mein 8 counters, ek mein 6. Pehla frame bharne ke liye counters khiskao. Doosre mein kitne bache, aur kul kitne?
hints: The first frame needs how many to be full?
Move 2 from the second frame.
Second frame has ___ left; total 10 + ___.
4 are left, so the total is 10 + 4 = 14.

items.prompt_en: You have ₹9 and Nani gives you ₹7. How much money do you have now?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare paas ₹9 hain aur Nani ₹7 deti hain. Ab tumhare paas kitne paise hain?
hints: 9 needs how many to make 10?
Take 1 from the 7. What is left?
10 and ___ make ___.
₹16 — 9 + 1 = 10, and 6 more make 16.

items.prompt_en: Teach Chintu how to do 7 + 5 by making 10 first.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao 7 + 5 pehle 10 banakar kaise karein.
items.answer: 7 needs 3 to make 10; break 5 into 3 and 2; 7 + 3 = 10, then 10 + 2 = 12
hints: What does Chintu need to add to 7 to make 10?
Where does he get those from?
7 needs 3; split 5 into 3 and 2; 10 + 2 = 12.

items.prompt_en: 10 and 7 more make?
items.prompt_hi: 10 aur 7 milkar kitne?
hints: One ten and some ones.
How many ones?
10 and 7 make ___.
17 — one ten and seven ones.

steps: Start with the bigger number, 8. It needs 2 more to make 10.
Break 5 into 2 and 3.
Give the 2 to the 8: 8 + 2 = 10.
Add what is left: 10 + 3 = 13.

skills.title: Counts back within 20
Uses the related addition fact to subtract (think addition)
Subtracts through 10 (13 − 5: back to 10, then the rest)
Knows taking all the ones from a teen leaves 10

expectations: Subtract by counting back, or by asking "what adds on to make the total?"
Go back to 10 first, then take away the rest
In 13 − 5 we take 5 from all 13, not do 5 − 3 with the digits
Check by adding back: the answer plus the part taken should make the start number

misconceptions.belief: Subtracts the smaller digit from the bigger one, so 13 − 5 gives 12
signs: Answers 12 for 13 − 5 and 12 for 14 − 6
Answer is bigger than 10 when it should be less

diagnostic.prompt_en: For 13 − 5, Riya says 8 and Sonu says 12. Who is right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 13 − 5 ke liye Riya kehti hai 8 aur Sonu kehta hai 12. Kaun sahi hai?

remediation.representation: Bundle and loose sticks: 13 is a bundle and 3; to take 5, untie the bundle
remediation.moveShape: Ask whether the answer should be more or less than 10 before calculating, then check with sticks

misconceptions.belief: Subtracts ones from ones and forgets the ten, so 16 − 6 gives 0
signs: Says 16 − 6 = 0
Ignores the bundle in teen subtraction

diagnostic.prompt_hi: 16 − 6 kitna?

remediation.representation: Full ten-frame plus 6 loose counters; remove the 6 loose ones and the full frame is still there
remediation.moveShape: Take away only the loose ones and ask what is still on the mat

misconceptions.belief: When counting back, counts the starting number as the first step and gets one too many
signs: For 12 − 3 counts "12, 11, 10" and says 10
Answers are one more than correct

diagnostic.prompt_en: For 12 − 3, Bholu counts back "12, 11, 10" and says 10. Is he right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 12 − 3 ke liye Bholu ulta ginta hai "12, 11, 10" aur kehta hai 10. Kya woh sahi hai?

remediation.representation: Number-line hops backwards with each landing spot marked
remediation.moveShape: Fold a finger for each new number said; the start number gets no finger

items.prompt_en: The sabziwala has 15 brinjals. He sells 1. How many are left?
items.prompt_hi: Sabziwale ke paas 15 baingan hain. Usne 1 becha. Kitne bache?
hints: One less than 15?
Count back one step from 15.
15 take away 1 is ___.
14 brinjals are left.

items.prompt_hi: 16 − 6 kitna?
hints: 16 is one ten and 6 ones.
Take away the 6 ones. What is still there?
The ___ is left.
10 — take away the 6 loose ones and the ten is left.

items.prompt_en: 13 − 5: first take 3 to reach 10, then take 2 more. What is the answer?
items.prompt_hi: 13 − 5: pehle 3 hatao taaki 10 ho jaaye, phir 2 aur hatao. Jawaab kya?
hints: 13 take away 3 is...?
Then take 2 more from 10.
8 — back to 10, then 2 more gives 8.
Start at 8 and count up to 15.
8 needs 2 to make 10, then 5 more.
2 and 5 make ___.
7 — because 8 + 7 = 15.

items.prompt_en: Count back 3 from 12. Where do you land?
items.prompt_hi: 12 se 3 peeche gino. Kahan pahunche?
hints: Say 12 in your head. Now 3 new numbers going back.
The first number back is 11.

items.prompt_en: 15 − 6. Guess first: will the answer be more than 10 or less than 10?
items.prompt_hi: 15 − 6. Pehle guess karo: jawaab 10 se zyada hoga ya kam?
hints: 15 is 10 and 5. You are taking away 6.
Is 6 more than the 5 loose ones?
Taking more than 5 goes below ___.
Less than 10 — taking 6 uses all 5 loose ones and 1 from the ten, leaving 9.

items.prompt_en: How does 9 + 6 = 15 help you find 15 − 6?
items.prompt_hi: 9 + 6 = 15 se 15 − 6 nikaalne mein kaise madad milti hai?
items.answer: If 9 and 6 make 15, taking the 6 away leaves 9
hints: 15 is made of which two parts?
If one part goes away, what stays?
9 — 15 is 9 and 6, so taking 6 away leaves 9.

items.prompt_en: Bholu says 14 − 6 = 12 because 6 − 4 = 2. Check his answer.
items.prompt_hi: Bholu kehta hai 14 − 6 = 12, kyunki 6 − 4 = 2. Uska jawaab check karo.
hints: Should taking 6 from 14 leave more than 10, or less?
Go back to 10 first: 14 − 4.
Bholu flipped the digits — 14 − 6 is 8. Check: 8 + 6 = 14.

items.prompt_en: 17 − 4 and 14 − 7: same answer or different?
items.prompt_hi: 17 − 4 aur 14 − 7: jawaab same hai ya alag?
hints: Work out 17 − 4 first.
Now 14 − 7: back to 10, then 3 more.
Different — 13 and 7. Swapping digits changes the problem.

items.prompt_en: The sabziwala had 15 brinjals and sold 6. How many are left?
items.prompt_hi: Sabziwale ke paas 15 baingan the, usne 6 beche. Kitne bache?
hints: Take 5 first to reach 10.
Then 1 more.
9 brinjals are left.

items.prompt_en: On a number line, start at 18 and jump back 5. Where do you land?
items.prompt_hi: Number line pe 18 se shuru karo aur 5 jump peeche. Kahan pahunche?
hints: Finger on 18. First jump lands on 17.
Keep going: 16, 15...
You land on 13.

items.prompt_en: A bus has 20 seats. 12 people are sitting. How many seats are empty?
items.prompt_hi: Bus mein 20 seats hain. 12 log baithe hain. Kitni seats khaali hain?
hints: Start at 12 and count up to 20.
12 to 20: how many steps?
12 and ___ make 20.
8 empty seats — 12 + 8 = 20.

items.prompt_en: Teach Chintu how to do 12 − 4 by going back to 10 first.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao 12 − 4 pehle 10 tak wapas jaakar kaise karein.
items.answer: Take 2 to get from 12 to 10, then take the other 2 from 10: 10 − 2 = 8
hints: How far is 12 from 10?
He takes 2 first. How many more of the 4 are left to take?

items.prompt_hi: 19 − 9 kitna?
hints: 19 is one ten and 9 ones.
Take away the 9 ones.
The ___ is left.

steps: 13 is 10 and 3. We need to take away 5.
Take away 3 first to get back to 10: 13 − 3 = 10.
We still need to take 2 more (because 3 + 2 = 5).
fadedVersion: We still need to take ___ more.

skills.title: Compares two lengths by lining up the ends
Orders three things by length or height
Uses comparison words: longer, shorter, taller, tallest
Reasons that if A is longer than B and B is longer than C, A is longer than C

expectations: Line up the ends at the same starting point before comparing
The one that goes further at the other end is longer
A bent or wiggly thing must be straightened to compare its length
Thick or fat does not mean long

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the object that sticks out further is longer even when the ends are not lined up
signs: Picks the pencil pushed forward as longer
Compares heights without a common floor level

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two pencils lie side by side. One is pushed ahead, so its tip sticks out more. Is it longer?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Do pencil saath mein rakhi hain. Ek ko aage khiska diya, to uski nok zyada bahar hai. Kya woh lambi hai?

options.text: We cannot tell until we line up the ends

remediation.representation: Start-line strip: both objects slide back to a red start line before comparing
remediation.moveShape: Slide both objects back to the start line, then compare the far ends

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a wiggly or bent string is shorter than the same string held straight
signs: Says a curled ribbon is shorter after it is curled
Judges length by end-to-end distance only

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two ribbons are exactly the same. I make one wiggly like a snake. Which one is longer now?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Do ribbon bilkul ek jaise hain. Main ek ko saanp jaisa tedha-medha kar deti hoon. Ab lamba kaun hai?

remediation.representation: Pull the wiggly ribbon straight beside the other one
remediation.moveShape: Predict, then straighten it in front of the child and compare from the same start

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a thicker or fatter object is longer
signs: Picks the fat short candle as longer
Uses "bada" for both long and thick

diagnostic.prompt_en: A fat short candle and a thin long candle. Which one is longer?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek moti chhoti mombatti aur ek patli lambi mombatti. Lambi kaun hai?

options.text: The fat one, because it is bigger

remediation.representation: Stand both on a start line and draw a line across the tops
remediation.moveShape: Ask "which is thicker?" and "which is longer?" as two questions with different answers

items.prompt_en: A pencil and a crayon lie side by side with their ends together. The pencil goes further. Which is longer?
items.prompt_hi: Pencil aur crayon saath mein rakhe hain, ek taraf ke sire barabar. Pencil aage tak jaati hai. Lamba kaun hai?
hints: The starting ends are together. Look at the other ends.
Which one reaches further?
The one that goes further is ___.
The pencil is longer.

items.prompt_en: Papa and Lina stand back to back. Papa's head is higher. Who is taller?
items.prompt_hi: Papa aur Lina peeth se peeth milaakar khade hain. Papa ka sar upar hai. Lamba kaun hai?
hints: They both stand on the same floor.
Whose head is higher?
The taller one is ___.
Papa is taller; Lina is shorter.

items.prompt_en: Dadi, Papa and Lina. Papa is the tallest and Lina is the shortest. Say them from tallest to shortest.
items.prompt_hi: Dadi, Papa aur Lina. Papa sabse lambe hain aur Lina sabse chhoti. Sabse lambe se sabse chhote tak bolo.
hints: Who goes first — the tallest.
Who goes last — the shortest.
Papa, ___, Lina.
Papa, Dadi, Lina.

items.prompt_en: Two pencils are exactly the same. I push one forward a little. Guess: is one longer now?
items.prompt_hi: Do pencil bilkul ek jaisi hain. Main ek ko thoda aage khiska deti hoon. Guess karo: kya ab ek lambi hai?
items.answer: No, they are still the same length
hints: Did I cut or stretch either pencil?
What happens if we line up their ends again?
Pushing it only moves it; the length stays ___.
No — they are still the same; one is just ahead.

items.prompt_en: Why must we put the ends together at the start before comparing?
items.prompt_hi: Compare karne se pehle shuru ke sire barabar kyun karne chahiye?
items.answer: So the comparison is fair; otherwise one can look longer just because it is ahead
hints: What if one pencil starts ahead of the other?
Could a shorter one then look longer?
Same start makes it ___.
A shared start line makes it fair; otherwise being ahead looks like being longer.

items.prompt_en: A thick short candle and a thin long candle. Which is longer?
items.prompt_hi: Ek moti chhoti mombatti aur ek patli lambi mombatti. Kaun lambi hai?
hints: Thick and long are different things.
Stand them on the table. Whose top is higher?
The ___ candle reaches higher.
The thin candle is longer, even though the other is thicker.

items.prompt_en: Two ribbons are exactly the same. I make one wiggly like a snake. Guess: which is longer now?
items.prompt_hi: Do ribbon bilkul ek jaise hain. Main ek ko saanp jaisa tedha kar deti hoon. Guess karo: ab lamba kaun hai?
hints: Did I cut any ribbon?
If I pull the wiggly one straight, what will we see?
Wiggly or straight, the length is the ___.
Same — making it wiggly does not make it shorter.

items.prompt_en: Bholu put one stick on a step and a longer stick on the floor. He says the one on the step is taller. Is that fair?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu ne ek lakdi seedhi pe rakhi aur ek lambi lakdi zameen pe. Woh kehta hai seedhi wali lambi hai. Kya yeh theek tareeka hai?
items.answer: No — both must start from the same level
hints: Do both sticks start at the same place?
The step lifts one stick up.
To compare, both must start on the ___ level.
Not fair — put both on the floor first, then compare.

items.prompt_en: Meenu and Riya are the same height. Meenu's plait reaches her waist. Riya's plait reaches her shoulder. Whose plait is longer?
items.prompt_hi: Meenu aur Riya ek jitni lambi hain. Meenu ki choti kamar tak aati hai. Riya ki choti kandhe tak. Kiski choti lambi hai?
hints: Both plaits start at the head.
Which is further down: waist or shoulder?
The plait reaching the ___ is longer.
Meenu's plait is longer — it goes down further.

items.prompt_en: Snake A is longer than snake B. Snake B is longer than snake C. Which snake is the shortest?
items.prompt_hi: Saanp A, saanp B se lamba hai. Saanp B, saanp C se lamba hai. Sabse chhota kaun hai?
hints: Put A and B in order first.
Now where does C go?
A, then B, then ___.
Snake C is the shortest.

items.prompt_en: Show with your hands how long a pencil is. Now show a cricket bat. For which one are your hands further apart?
items.prompt_hi: Haathon se dikhao pencil kitni lambi hai. Ab cricket bat dikhao. Kiske liye haath zyada door hain?
hints: Hold your hands for a pencil.
Now open them for a bat.
Hands go further apart for the ___.
The bat — it is longer than a pencil.

items.prompt_en: Will a new mat fit along the wall? How can you check without carrying the mat to the wall?
items.prompt_hi: Kya nayi chatai deewar ke saath fit hogi? Chatai ko deewar tak le jaaye bina kaise check karoge?
items.answer: Use a string or stick: mark the mat's length on it, then hold it along the wall
hints: Is there something you could carry instead of the mat?
A string can be as long as the mat.
Mark the mat on a ___, then compare it with the wall.
Lay a string along the mat, mark it, then hold the string against the wall.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to find which of two ropes is longer.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao do rassiyon mein se lambi kaun si hai, kaise pata kare.
items.answer: Straighten both, line up one end at the same start, and see which goes further at the other end
hints: What should Chintu do if a rope is curled?
Where should both ropes start?
Straighten, line up the ___, see which goes ___.
Straighten both, start them together, and the one that goes further is longer.

items.prompt_en: Who is taller: a giraffe or a goat?
items.prompt_hi: Lamba kaun hai: jiraaf ya bakri?
hints: Picture them standing side by side.
Whose head is higher?
The taller one is the ___.
The giraffe is taller.

workedExample.problem: Which is longer: the red ribbon or the blue ribbon?
steps: Straighten both ribbons.
Put one end of each on the same start line.
Look at the other ends. The blue one goes further.
So the blue ribbon is longer.
fadedVersion: Put one end of each on the same ___.
Look at the other ends: the blue one goes ___.

skills.title: Measures by laying units end to end with no gaps or overlaps and counting them
Knows a bigger unit gives a smaller count
Compares two measurements only when the same unit is used

expectations: Put the units end to end with no gaps and no overlaps
Count how many units fit: that number is the length in those units
A bigger unit gives a smaller number
To compare lengths, both must be measured with the same unit

misconceptions.belief: Believes the number of hand-spans will be the same no matter whose hand is used
signs: Predicts Papa will get the same count as the child
Is surprised when counts differ

diagnostic.prompt_en: Lina measures the mat: 6 of her hand-spans. Papa measures the same mat with his bigger hand. Will he get more, fewer, or 6?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Lina ne chatai naapi: uske 6 baalisht. Papa usi chatai ko apne bade haath se naapte hain. Unke zyada aayenge, kam, ya 6?

remediation.representation: Side-by-side strips: the mat tiled with small spans and with big spans
remediation.moveShape: Measure the same object with two units in front of the child and line the two tilings up

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a bigger unit gives a bigger number
signs: Says the long stick will give a bigger count than the pencil
Associates "big" with "big number"

diagnostic.prompt_en: We measure a table with a pencil and with a long stick. Which gives the smaller number?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Hum ek table ko pencil se aur ek lambi lakdi se naapte hain. Kisse chhota number aayega?

remediation.representation: Tiling animation: big units cover the table in fewer pieces
remediation.moveShape: Predict, measure both ways, then ask why fewer sticks fit

misconceptions.belief: Thinks gaps or overlaps between units do not matter, as long as every unit is counted
signs: Leaves spaces between matchboxes
Overlaps hand-spans and counts each one

diagnostic.prompt_en: Bholu measured a table with matchboxes but left big gaps between them. Is his count right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Bholu ne maachis ki dibbiyon se table naapi par beech mein bade gap chhod diye. Kya uski ginti sahi hai?

options.text: No — gaps make the count too small

remediation.representation: Ghost boxes appear in the gaps showing the units that are missing
remediation.moveShape: Fill the gaps with more units and recount

items.prompt_en: A book is as long as 3 crayons laid end to end. How long is the book in crayons?
items.prompt_hi: Ek kitaab 3 crayon ek ke baad ek rakhne jitni lambi hai. Kitaab kitne crayon lambi hai?
hints: How many crayons fit along the book?
Count them.
The book is ___ crayons long.
3 crayons long.

items.prompt_en: You walk from the door to the bed: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 footsteps, heel touching toe. How long is it?
items.prompt_hi: Tum darwaaze se bistar tak chalte ho: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 kadam, aedi se panja milaakar. Kitni doori hai?
hints: Count the steps.
What was the last number?
It is ___ footsteps.
5 footsteps.

items.prompt_en: Lina's mat is 6 of her hand-spans. Papa's hand is bigger. Guess: will Papa count more or fewer than 6?
items.prompt_hi: Lina ki chatai uske 6 baalisht ki hai. Papa ka haath bada hai. Guess karo: Papa ke 6 se zyada aayenge ya kam?
hints: Each of Papa's spans covers more of the mat.
If each piece is bigger, do we need more or fewer pieces?
Bigger spans means ___ spans.
Fewer — Papa's bigger span covers more each time.

items.prompt_en: Why does Papa get fewer hand-spans than Lina on the same mat?
items.prompt_hi: Ek hi chatai pe Papa ke baalisht Lina se kam kyun aate hain?
items.answer: His hand-span is longer, so fewer of them fit along the mat
hints: Compare Papa's span with Lina's.
If each span is longer, how many fit?
His span is ___, so ___ fit.
Papa's span is longer, so fewer spans fit along the same mat.

items.prompt_en: We measure the table with a pencil and with a long stick. Which gives the smaller number?
items.prompt_hi: Table ko pencil se aur lambi lakdi se naapte hain. Kisse chhota number aayega?
hints: Which unit is bigger?
Bigger units need more or fewer to cover the table?
The ___ gives the smaller number.
The long stick — fewer sticks fit.

items.prompt_en: Bholu laid matchboxes with big gaps between them and counted 4. Is the table really 4 matchboxes long?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu ne maachis ki dibbiyaan bade gap ke saath rakhi aur 4 gini. Kya table sach mein 4 dibbi lambi hai?
items.answer: No — the gaps make the count too small; more matchboxes would fit
hints: What should be between the matchboxes?
If we fill the gaps, will we need more boxes?
No gaps, so the real count is ___ than 4.
No — the gaps hide extra matchboxes; the table is longer than 4.

items.prompt_en: Using the same hand, the desk is 5 hand-spans and the chair is 3 hand-spans. Which is longer?
items.prompt_hi: Ek hi haath se desk 5 baalisht aur kursi 3 baalisht hai. Lamba kaun hai?
hints: Same hand, so the unit is the same.
Which number is more?
5 is more than 3, so the ___ is longer.
The desk — 5 spans is more than 3.

items.prompt_en: The corridor is 8 of your footsteps. The room is 6 of your footsteps. How many more steps is the corridor?
items.prompt_hi: Gali tumhare 8 kadam ki hai. Kamra tumhare 6 kadam ka. Gali kitne kadam zyada hai?
hints: Same feet, so we can compare.
Count up from 6 to 8.
2 more footsteps.

items.prompt_en: Stretch your thumb and little finger apart: that is one hand-span. How would you measure your notebook with it?
items.prompt_hi: Angootha aur chhoti ungli failaao: yeh ek baalisht hai. Isse apni copy kaise naapoge?
items.answer: Put the span at one end, then put the next span where the last one ended, with no gaps, and count the spans
hints: Where do you start the first span?
Where does the second span begin?
Start at the ___, no ___, then count.
Start at one edge, place each span where the last ended, no gaps, and count them.

items.prompt_en: Riya says her room is 10 footsteps. Arjun says his room is 8 footsteps. Can we be sure Riya's room is longer?
items.prompt_hi: Riya kehti hai uska kamra 10 kadam ka hai. Arjun kehta hai uska 8 kadam ka. Kya pakka hai ki Riya ka kamra lamba hai?
items.answer: No — their feet may be different sizes; we need the same unit to compare
hints: Whose feet were used for each room?
Are their feet the same size?
To compare, we need the ___ unit.
Not sure — different feet are different units. Measure both rooms with the same feet.

items.prompt_en: If your hand-spans overlap each other, will you get a bigger or a smaller count than the true one?
items.prompt_hi: Agar tumhare baalisht ek doosre ke upar chadh jaayein, to sahi ginti se zyada aayegi ya kam?
items.answer: Bigger — each span covers less new length, so you need more spans
hints: When spans overlap, does each one cover a full span of new length?
If each covers less, do you need more or fewer?
Overlapping means ___ spans.
A bigger count — overlapping wastes length, so more spans are needed.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to measure the bed with his footsteps.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao apne kadmon se bistar kaise naape.
items.answer: Start at one end, put heel to toe each step with no gaps, walk to the other end, and count the steps
hints: Where does Chintu start?
How should each foot touch the last?
Start at the end, ___ to ___, then count.
Start at one end, heel touching toe, no gaps, and count the steps to the other end.

items.prompt_en: The same rug is measured with a small spoon and with a big ladle. Which gives the bigger number?
items.prompt_hi: Ek hi dari ko chhote chammach se aur badi karchi se naapa. Kisse bada number aayega?
hints: Which is the smaller unit?
Small units need more or fewer?
The smaller unit gives the ___ number.
The spoon — smaller units need more of them.

workedExample.problem: How long is the dining mat in your hand-spans?
steps: Put your thumb at one end of the mat and stretch your little finger.
Move your thumb to where your little finger was — no gap, no overlap.
Keep going to the other end, counting: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
The mat is 6 of your hand-spans long.
fadedVersion: Put your thumb at one ___ of the mat.
Move your thumb to where your little finger was — no ___.
Keep counting to the other end: 1, 2, ___...
The mat is ___ of your hand-spans long.

skills.title: Compares weights by lifting
Reads a simple balance: the lower side is heavier
Knows size or number of things does not decide weight

expectations: The heavier thing pulls its side of the balance down
The side that goes up is lighter
Bigger is not always heavier, and more things is not always heavier
If the balance stays level, both sides weigh the same

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the bigger object is always heavier
signs: Picks a big pillow as heavier than a small brick
Uses "bada" to mean heavy

diagnostic.prompt_en: A big pillow or a small brick — which is heavier?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek bada takiya ya ek chhoti eent — bhaari kaun hai?

options.text: The pillow, because it is bigger

remediation.representation: Balance sim with a big light object and a small heavy one
remediation.moveShape: Predict, then lift both (or test on the balance) and talk about the surprise

misconceptions.belief: Misreads the balance: thinks the side that goes up is heavier
signs: Says the leaf is heavier because its side went up
Links "up" with "more"

diagnostic.prompt_en: On a balance, the apple side goes down and the leaf side goes up. Which is heavier?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Taraazu mein seb wala palda neeche gaya aur patte wala upar. Bhaari kaun hai?

options.text: The leaf, because it went up

remediation.representation: Child holds a bag in each hand as a human balance and feels which hand sinks
remediation.moveShape: Use the body balance first, then map it onto the pan balance picture

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the side with more objects is always heavier
signs: Says 3 peas are heavier than 1 potato
Counts objects to decide weight

diagnostic.prompt_en: One side has 1 big potato. The other side has 3 small peas. The potato side goes down. Which is heavier?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek taraf 1 bada aaloo hai. Doosri taraf 3 chhote matar. Aaloo wala palda neeche jaata hai. Bhaari kaun hai?

options.text: The peas, because there are more of them

remediation.representation: Balance sim adding peas one at a time; the potato side stays down
remediation.moveShape: Keep adding small things and ask each time whether the balance changed

items.prompt_en: A school bag full of books, or a feather. Which is heavier?
items.prompt_hi: Kitaabon se bhara school bag, ya ek pankh. Bhaari kaun hai?
hints: Imagine lifting each one.
Which would make your arm work harder?
The heavier one is the ___.
The full school bag is heavier.

items.prompt_en: On the balance, the mango side goes down. Which is heavier: the mango or the leaf on the other side?
items.prompt_hi: Taraazu mein aam wala palda neeche gaya. Bhaari kaun hai: aam ya doosri taraf ka patta?
hints: Which side went down?
The heavier thing pulls its side...?
Down means ___.
The mango is heavier — its side went down.

items.prompt_en: A big balloon or a small stone: which is lighter?
items.prompt_hi: Ek bada gubbara ya ek chhota patthar: halka kaun hai?
hints: Imagine holding each.
Does a balloon feel heavy even though it is big?
The lighter one is the ___.
The balloon is lighter, even though it is bigger.

items.prompt_en: A big pillow and a small brick go on a balance. Guess which side will go down.
items.prompt_hi: Ek bada takiya aur ek chhoti eent taraazu pe rakhe. Guess karo kaun sa palda neeche jaayega?
hints: Which one is big? Which one is heavy?
Is big the same as heavy?
The ___ is heavier, so its side goes down.
The brick side goes down — the brick is small but heavy.

items.prompt_en: Why does the heavier side of a balance go down?
items.prompt_hi: Taraazu ka bhaari palda neeche kyun jaata hai?
items.answer: The heavier thing pulls or presses down more
hints: Hold something heavy in your hand. What does your hand do?
Heavy things press down...
The heavier thing ___ down more.
The heavier thing presses down harder, so its side sinks.

items.prompt_en: A pumpkin is on one side and 5 potatoes are on the other. The balance stays level. What does that tell us?
items.prompt_hi: Ek taraf kaddu hai aur doosri taraf 5 aaloo. Taraazu barabar rehta hai. Isse kya pata chalta hai?
hints: Did either side go down?
Level means neither side is heavier.
Level means they weigh the ___.
The pumpkin and the 5 potatoes weigh the same.

items.prompt_en: Bholu sees the onion side go up and says the onion is heavier. Is he right?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu dekhta hai pyaaz wala palda upar gaya aur kehta hai pyaaz bhaari hai. Kya woh sahi hai?
items.answer: No — the side that goes up is lighter; the onion is lighter
hints: Which way does a heavy thing push the pan?
The onion side went up. What does up mean?
Up means ___.
Bholu is wrong — the onion went up, so it is the lighter one.

items.prompt_en: A big empty basket or a small brick: which is heavier to carry?
items.prompt_hi: Ek badi khaali tokri ya ek chhoti eent: uthaane mein bhaari kaun hai?
hints: The basket is big but what is inside it?
Picture lifting the brick.
The ___ is heavier.
The brick — the big basket is empty and light.

items.prompt_en: One big potato is on one side and 3 small peas are on the other. The potato side goes down. Which is heavier?
items.prompt_hi: Ek taraf 1 bada aaloo aur doosri taraf 3 chhote matar. Aaloo wala palda neeche gaya. Bhaari kaun hai?
hints: Which side went down?
Does having more things mean heavier?
Down means ___, so the potato is heavier.
The potato — even 3 peas are lighter than one potato.

items.prompt_en: Be a balance! Hold a book in one hand and a pencil in the other. Which hand goes down?
items.prompt_hi: Taraazu ban jao! Ek haath mein kitaab aur doosre mein pencil pakdo. Kaun sa haath neeche jaata hai?
hints: Hold both arms out straight.
Which hand feels a stronger pull?
The ___ hand goes down.
The book hand — the book is heavier.

items.prompt_en: Two bags of the same size from the market: one full of tomatoes, one full of puffed rice (murmura). Which is easier to carry?
items.prompt_hi: Bazaar se ek jaise size ke do thaile: ek mein tamatar bhare hain, ek mein murmura. Kaun sa uthaana aasaan hai?
items.answer: the puffed rice bag — it is lighter
hints: Same size bags. Which filling is heavier?
Think about holding a handful of each.
The lighter bag is the ___ bag.
The murmura bag is lighter and easier to carry.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to use a see-saw balance to find which of two things is heavier.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao do cheezon mein bhaari kaun hai, yeh jhoole jaise taraazu se kaise pata kare.
items.answer: Put one thing on each side; the side that goes down is heavier; if it stays level they weigh the same
hints: Where does Chintu put the two things?
Then what does he watch for?
The side that goes ___ is heavier; level means ___.
One thing on each side: the side that sinks is heavier; level means the same weight.

items.prompt_en: Remember the pillow and the brick? Is the bigger thing always heavier?
items.prompt_hi: Takiya aur eent yaad hai? Kya badi cheez hamesha bhaari hoti hai?
items.answer: No — a big thing can be light and a small thing can be heavy
hints: Which was bigger, the pillow or the brick?
Which was heavier?
Big is ___ always heavy.
No — the small brick was heavier than the big pillow.

workedExample.problem: Which is heavier: a big pillow or a small brick?
steps: Put the pillow on one side of the balance and the brick on the other.
Watch: the brick side goes down and the pillow side goes up.
The side that goes down holds the heavier thing.
So the brick is heavier, even though it is smaller.
fadedVersion: Put one thing on each ___ of the balance.
The side that goes down is ___.

skills.title: Groups objects into tens and ones and counts the tens and the ones
Writes the two-digit number from tens and ones (46, not 406)
Reads a two-digit number as tens and ones
Counts in tens: 10, 20, 30 ... 90

expectations: Make bundles of 10 and count the bundles, then the loose ones
The left digit tells how many tens, the right digit tells how many ones
46 is 4 tens and 6 ones and is written 46, not 406
A 0 in the ones place means no loose ones, like 30

misconceptions.belief: Writes forty-six as 406 (writes the tens as 40 then the 6)
signs: Writes 406 for forty-six, 702 for seventy-two
Says each part aloud and writes each part

diagnostic.prompt_en: Forty-six is 4 tens and 6 ones. Which is right: 46 or 406?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Forty-six (chhiyaalees) matlab 4 das aur 6 ekaai. Sahi kaun hai: 46 ya 406?

remediation.representation: Arrow cards: the 6 card slides over the 0 of the 40 card
remediation.moveShape: Lay the ones card on top of the zero to show the zero is "covered" by the 6

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the 4 in 46 means just 4, not 40
signs: Shows 4 sticks for the 4 in 46
Says 46 is "4 and 6, so 10"

diagnostic.prompt_en: In 46, how many sticks does the 4 stand for?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 46 mein 4 kitni teeliyon ke liye hai?

remediation.representation: Bundles of ten on a place-value mat; untie one bundle to show 10 inside
remediation.moveShape: Build the number with bundles and ask how many sticks the left digit covers

How many bundles, and how many left over?

expectations: A pattern has a part that repeats again and again: the core

Star — after the star comes moon, then star again.

What comes after moon?

acceptable: roti dal chawal roti dal chawal

Now say the core again.
Roti, dal, chawal, ___, ___, ___.
Roti, dal, chawal, roti, dal, chawal.

items.prompt_en: Design a rangoli border for Diwali using diyas and flowers. Tell me the rule and the first 6 pieces.
items.prompt_hi: Diwali ke liye diye aur phoolon se rangoli ka border banao. Rule aur pehle 6 cheezein batao.
items.answer: Any clear rule with a core repeated, e.g. "diya, flower, flower": diya, flower, flower, diya, flower, flower
acceptable: diya flower diya flower diya flower
diya flower flower diya flower flower
hints: First choose your core.
Then repeat it without changing it.
Rule: ___. First 6: ___.
For example, rule "diya, flower": diya, flower, diya, flower, diya, flower.

items.prompt_en: Teach Chintu how to make his own pattern.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao apna khud ka pattern kaise banaye.
items.answer: Choose a core, repeat the whole core again and again without changing it, and say the rule out loud
hints: What does Chintu choose first?
What does he do with it?
Choose a ___, ___ it, and say the ___.
Pick a core, keep repeating it the same way, and tell the rule.

items.prompt_en: Is "clap, jump, clap, jump" a pattern?
items.prompt_hi: Kya "taali, kood, taali, kood" ek pattern hai?
hints: Does any part repeat?
Clap, jump... then?
Clap, jump ___.
Yes — clap, jump repeats.

items.prompt_en: Is "red, blue" on its own a pattern, or must it repeat?
items.prompt_hi: Kya akela "laal, neela" pattern hai, ya use repeat hona padega?
items.answer: It must repeat — red, blue, red, blue... makes a pattern
hints: With only red, blue, can you guess what comes next?
A pattern lets you guess the next piece.
It must ___.
It must repeat — once is just the core.

workedExample.problem: Make a mala pattern with red and yellow beads and tell the rule.
steps: Choose a core: red, red, yellow.
Put the core on the string: red, red, yellow.
Repeat the whole core again: red, red, yellow, red, red, yellow.
Say the rule: two red, then one yellow, again and again.
fadedVersion: Put the core on the string.
Rule: ___ red, then ___ yellow, again and again.

skills.title: Orders daily activities: first, next, last
Uses before and after correctly
Names parts of the day in order: morning, afternoon, evening, night
Tells yesterday from tomorrow

expectations: Some things always happen before others (brush teeth before nashta)
Before means earlier; after means later — whatever order the words are said in
The day goes morning, afternoon, evening, night
Yesterday has already gone; tomorrow is still coming (in Hindi both are "kal", so the sentence tells which)

misconceptions.belief: Thinks "yesterday" and "tomorrow" mean the same thing (in Hindi both are "kal")
signs: Says "I will go yesterday"
Cannot tell whether "kal" means past or future from the sentence

diagnostic.prompt_en: "Kal hum mela jaayenge." Is the mela trip yesterday or tomorrow?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: "Kal hum mela jaayenge." Mela jaana beete hue kal hai ya aane waale kal?

options.text: Tomorrow — "jaayenge" means it has not happened yet

remediation.representation: Three-day strip: yesterday (done, ticked), today (now), tomorrow (coming, with an arrow)
remediation.moveShape: Point at the strip while asking "has it happened yet?" and listen for the verb ending

misconceptions.belief: Does things in the order they are said, not the order "before/after" tells
signs: For "Before you eat, wash your hands" says eat comes first
Follows sentence order with "after" sentences

diagnostic.prompt_en: "Before you eat, wash your hands." What do you do first?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: "Khaane se pehle haath dho lo." Pehle kya karoge?

remediation.representation: Two picture cards placed on a first-then strip as the sentence is unpacked
remediation.moveShape: Have the child place the cards on the strip before acting out the sentence

items.prompt_en: What do you do first: brush your teeth or eat nashta?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle kya karte ho: daant brush ya nashta?
hints: Think about your morning.
Do we eat with an unbrushed mouth?
First I ___.
Brush teeth first, then nashta.

items.prompt_en: When do we sleep: in the morning or at night?
items.prompt_hi: Hum kab sote hain: subah ya raat ko?
hints: When is it dark outside?
When do you go to bed?
We sleep at ___.
At night.

items.prompt_en: Put in order: go to school, sleep at night, wake up.
items.prompt_hi: Order mein lagao: school jaana, raat ko sona, uthna.
items.answer: wake up, go to school, sleep at night
hints: What is the very first thing in your day?
What is the very last?
Wake up, ___, ___.
Wake up, go to school, sleep at night.

items.prompt_en: "Before you eat, wash your hands." What do you do first?
items.prompt_hi: "Khaane se pehle haath dho lo." Pehle kya karoge?
hints: "Before you eat" — so eating comes...?
Which job happens earlier?
First ___, then eat.
Wash your hands first, then eat.

items.prompt_en: "Take a bath after you play." Which comes first, the bath or playing?
items.prompt_hi: "Khelne ke baad naha lena." Pehle kya hoga, nahaana ya khelna?
hints: "After you play" — so playing is...?
Bath is after what?
First ___, then bath.
Playing comes first; the bath is after.

items.prompt_en: The sun is going down and the sky is orange. Guess what comes next: night or morning?
items.prompt_hi: Sooraj doob raha hai aur aasmaan naarangi hai. Guess karo aage kya aayega: raat ya subah?
hints: Is this the start of the day or the end?
After evening comes...?
Evening, then ___.
Night comes next.

items.prompt_en: Why do we put on socks before shoes?
items.prompt_hi: Hum joote se pehle mozze kyun pehente hain?
items.answer: Socks go inside the shoes; you cannot put socks on over shoes
hints: Where do socks go when you wear shoes?
Could you pull a sock over a shoe?
Socks go ___ the shoes.
Socks go inside the shoes, so they must go on first.

items.prompt_en: "Kal" can mean yesterday or tomorrow. In "kal hum mela jaayenge", which does it mean?
items.prompt_hi: "Kal" ka matlab beeta hua kal bhi hota hai aur aane wala kal bhi. "Kal hum mela jaayenge" mein kaun sa?
hints: Has the mela trip happened yet?
"Jaayenge" means we will go.
Will go means ___.
Tomorrow — "jaayenge" tells us it is still coming.

items.prompt_en: Bholu says, "I will go to Nani's house yesterday." Which word is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu kehta hai, "I will go to Nani's house yesterday." Kaun sa shabd galat hai?
hints: "I will go" — has it happened yet?
Yesterday has already gone.
For something coming, we say ___.
"Yesterday" is wrong — "I will go" needs "tomorrow".

items.prompt_en: Making a roti: eat it, cook it on the tawa, roll the dough. Put these in order.
items.prompt_hi: Roti banana: khaana, tawe pe sekna, aata belna. Inhe order mein lagao.
items.answer: roll the dough, cook it on the tawa, eat it
hints: Can you eat a roti before it is cooked?
Can you cook it before rolling?
First ___, then ___, then eat.
Roll, cook, eat.

items.prompt_en: Two pictures: the sun rising, and the moon in a dark sky. Which picture goes with "subah" (morning)?
items.prompt_hi: Do tasveerein: ugta sooraj, aur andhere aasmaan mein chaand. "Subah" ke saath kaun si tasveer jaati hai?
hints: What do you see in the sky when you wake up?
When do we see the moon?
Morning goes with the ___.
The rising sun — that is morning.

items.prompt_en: The train leaves at night. Papa says, "Pack your bag before dinner." Is packing earlier or later than dinner?
items.prompt_hi: Train raat ko jaati hai. Papa kehte hain, "Dinner se pehle bag pack kar lo." Packing dinner se pehle hai ya baad?
hints: What does "before dinner" mean?
Before means...?
Packing is ___ than dinner.
Earlier — packing happens before dinner.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu what "before" and "after" mean, using your school day.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko apne school ke din se samjhao "pehle" aur "baad" ka matlab kya hai.
items.answer: Before means earlier, after means later — e.g., I eat nashta before school, I play after school
hints: What do you do before going to school?
What do you do after coming home?
Before means ___, after means ___.
Before means earlier (nashta before school); after means later (play after school).

items.prompt_en: What comes first: taking a bath or getting dressed?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle kya aata hai: nahaana ya kapde pehenna?
hints: Do you bathe with your clothes on?
Which one comes earlier?
First ___, then get dressed.
Bath first, then get dressed.

workedExample.problem: Put in order: eat nashta, wake up, go to school.
steps: Find the very first thing: wake up.
Ask what comes next: nashta comes before school.
The last one: go to school.
So: wake up, eat nashta, go to school.

skills.title: Compares how long two familiar activities take
Compares durations by counting (claps or numbers) while doing them
Knows how fun something feels does not change how long it takes

expectations: Takes longer means it lasts more time: you can count more while doing it
To compare fairly, start counting when each activity starts and stop when it ends
How fun something feels does not change how long it really takes
Going further or faster does not mean more time

misconceptions.belief: Believes an activity that is more fun takes less time
signs: Says the cartoon was shorter than homework when both took the same time
Judges time by how it felt

diagnostic.prompt_en: Playing for 20 counts and doing homework for 20 counts. Which took longer?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 20 ginti tak khelna aur 20 ginti tak homework. Kisme zyada time laga?

remediation.representation: Two sand-timer bars filling at the same rate for each activity
remediation.moveShape: Count aloud during both activities and compare the two numbers, not the feelings

misconceptions.belief: Thinks whoever goes further took more time, even if they started and stopped together
signs: Says the faster runner ran for longer
Mixes up "far" and "long time"

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya and Sonu start running together and stop together. Riya went further. Who ran for a longer time?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya aur Sonu ek saath daudna shuru karte hain aur ek saath rukte hain. Riya zyada door gayi. Kisne zyada der tak daud lagaayi?

remediation.representation: Timeline bars for each runner, both starting and ending at the same tick
remediation.moveShape: Separate "how far" and "how long": ask both questions and let the answers differ

items.prompt_en: Eating a banana or a long walk to school — which takes longer?
items.prompt_hi: Kela khaana ya school tak lamba paidal raasta — kisme zyada time lagta hai?
hints: How many bites is a banana?
How many steps is a long walk?
The ___ takes longer.
The long walk to school takes longer.

items.prompt_en: Blinking your eyes or taking a bath — which takes longer?
items.prompt_hi: Palak jhapakna ya nahaana — kisme zyada time lagta hai?
hints: Blink now. How quick was that?
Is a bath that quick?
The ___ takes longer.
A bath takes much longer than a blink.

items.prompt_en: Brushing teeth took 30 claps. Washing hands took 10 claps. Which took longer?
items.prompt_hi: Daant saaf karne mein 30 taaliyaan lagi. Haath dhone mein 10. Kisme zyada time laga?
hints: Which number of claps is more?
More claps means more time.
30 is more than 10, so ___ took longer.
Brushing teeth — 30 claps is more than 10.

items.prompt_en: Guess which takes longer: writing your name, or writing all the numbers from 1 to 20? Then we will count to check.
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo kisme zyada time lagega: apna naam likhna, ya 1 se 20 tak saare number likhna? Phir gin ke check karenge.
items.answer: writing 1 to 20 — there is much more to write
hints: How many letters is your name?
How many numbers from 1 to 20?
More to write means ___ time.
Writing 1 to 20 — there is far more to write.

items.prompt_en: How can counting help us know which activity takes longer?
items.prompt_hi: Ginti karne se kaise pata chalta hai kaun sa kaam zyada time leta hai?
items.answer: Count while each activity happens; the one where we count higher took longer
hints: What do we do while the activity is going on?
What does a bigger count tell us?
The activity with the ___ count took longer.
Count during each one — the bigger count took more time.

items.prompt_en: Playing cricket for 20 counts and doing homework for 20 counts. Which was longer?
items.prompt_hi: 20 ginti tak cricket khelna aur 20 ginti tak homework karna. Kaun lamba tha?
hints: What were the two counts?
Are 20 and 20 different?
Both were ___ counts.
The same — 20 counts each, even if cricket felt shorter.

items.prompt_en: Bholu says the cartoon was short because it was fun, and homework was long — but both took 15 minutes. What is right?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu kehta hai cartoon chhota tha kyunki mazedaar tha, aur homework lamba — par dono mein 15 minute lage. Sahi kya hai?
items.answer: Both took the same time; fun only made the cartoon feel shorter
hints: How many minutes did each take?
Does feeling fast change the clock?
Both took ___ minutes.
They took the same 15 minutes; fun only felt quicker.

items.prompt_en: Boiling milk on the stove or toasting a papad on the flame — which takes longer?
items.prompt_hi: Chulhe pe doodh ubaalna ya aanch pe papad sekna — kisme zyada time lagta hai?
hints: How fast does a papad crisp up?
Do we wait a while for milk to boil?
The ___ takes longer.
Boiling milk takes longer; a papad toasts in a few seconds.

items.prompt_en: Riya and Sonu start running together and stop together. Riya went further. Who ran for a longer time?
items.prompt_hi: Riya aur Sonu ek saath daudna shuru karte hain aur ek saath rukte hain. Riya zyada door gayi. Kisne zyada der daud lagaayi?
hints: Did they start at the same moment?
Did they stop at the same moment?
Same start and same stop means ___ time.
The same time — Riya was faster, so she went further in the same time.

items.prompt_en: You hopped on one foot while I counted to 8. Then you stood still while I counted to 12. Which lasted longer?
items.prompt_hi: Main 8 tak gini aur tum ek pair pe kood rahe the. Phir main 12 tak gini aur tum khade rahe. Kaun zyada der chala?
hints: Which count was bigger, 8 or 12?
A bigger count means more time.
12 is more than 8, so ___ lasted longer.
Standing still — 12 counts is longer than 8.

items.prompt_en: A long train trip to Nani's village or an auto-rickshaw ride to the market nearby — which usually takes longer?
items.prompt_hi: Nani ke gaon ki lambi train yatra ya paas ke bazaar tak auto ki sawaari — aam taur pe kisme zyada time lagta hai?
hints: Which place is further away?
Do you sleep or eat on the way to Nani's?
The ___ takes longer.
The long train trip takes longer than a short auto ride.

items.prompt_en: Tell Chintu how to find out which takes longer: drinking milk or eating a roti.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko batao kaise pata kare kisme zyada time lagta hai: doodh peena ya roti khaana.
items.answer: Count from when each one starts until it finishes; the one with the bigger count takes longer
hints: When should Chintu start counting?
When does he stop?
Count from ___ to ___; bigger count is longer.
Count from start to finish for each one; the bigger count took longer.

items.prompt_en: Which takes longer: a whole night's sleep or eating a toffee?
items.prompt_hi: Kisme zyada time lagta hai: poori raat ki neend ya ek toffee khaana?
hints: How long does a toffee last?
How long do you sleep?
The ___ takes longer.
A night's sleep — it lasts many hours.

workedExample.problem: Which takes longer: drinking a glass of water or eating a roti?
steps: Start counting when you start drinking. Stop when the glass is empty: say you reach 10.
Start counting again when you start eating the roti. Stop when it is finished: say you reach 60.
Compare the counts: 60 is more than 10.
So eating the roti takes longer.
fadedVersion: Count while eating the roti: you reach ___.

skills.title: Recognises equal groups (same number in each group)
Finds the total of equal groups by adding the same number again and again
Describes equal groups as "3 groups of 2"

expectations: Equal groups have the same number in each group
Add the group size once for each group
Count the things inside the groups, not the groups themselves
"4 groups of 2" means 2 + 2 + 2 + 2

misconceptions.belief: Counts groups instead of objects when asked how many in all
signs: Says 3 for "3 autos with 3 wheels each, how many wheels?"
Points at each group once

diagnostic.prompt_en: 3 auto-rickshaws, 3 wheels on each. How many wheels in all?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 3 auto-rickshaw, har ek mein 3 pahiye. Kul kitne pahiye?

remediation.representation: Groups drawn as circles with dots inside; tap each dot, not each circle
remediation.moveShape: Ask "how many autos?" then "how many wheels?" as two different questions

misconceptions.belief: Adds the number of groups and the number in each group (3 groups of 4 gives 3 + 4 = 7)
signs: Says 7 for 3 plates of 4 laddoos
Uses each number in the story once

diagnostic.prompt_en: 3 plates, 4 laddoos on each plate. How many laddoos?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 3 plates, har plate pe 4 laddoo. Kitne laddoo?

remediation.representation: Repeated-addition strip: one "+4" card for each plate
remediation.moveShape: Lay down one card per group and add along the cards

misconceptions.belief: Thinks groups with different numbers are still "equal groups"
signs: Calls plates of 2, 3 and 2 rotis equal groups
Uses repeated addition on unequal groups

diagnostic.prompt_en: Three plates have 2, 3 and 2 rotis. Are these equal groups?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Teen plates mein 2, 3 aur 2 rotiyaan hain. Kya yeh barabar group hain?

options.text: No — one plate has a different number

remediation.representation: Line the groups up in rows; the uneven row sticks out
remediation.moveShape: Have the child count each group aloud and compare the numbers

items.prompt_en: Three plates have 2, 2 and 2 laddoos. Is there the same number on each plate?
items.prompt_hi: Teen plates pe 2, 2 aur 2 laddoo hain. Kya har plate pe barabar hain?
hints: Count each plate.
Are all the numbers the same?
Each plate has ___.
Yes — 2 on every plate, so they are equal groups.

items.prompt_en: 2 plates, 2 laddoos on each. How many laddoos?
items.prompt_hi: 2 plates, har plate pe 2 laddoo. Kitne laddoo?
hints: Count the laddoos, not the plates.
2 and 2 more...
4 laddoos.

items.prompt_en: 3 auto-rickshaws, 3 wheels on each. How many wheels?
items.prompt_hi: 3 auto-rickshaw, har ek mein 3 pahiye. Kitne pahiye?
hints: Are we counting autos or wheels?
Add 3 for each auto.
9 wheels.

items.prompt_en: 4 + 4 + 4. How many groups of 4 is that?
items.prompt_hi: 4 + 4 + 4. Isme 4 ke kitne group hain?
hints: Count how many 4s you see.
Point to each 4.
There are ___ fours.
3 groups of 4.

items.prompt_en: 5 cycles, 2 wheels on each. Guess: more than 5 wheels or fewer?
items.prompt_hi: 5 cycle, har ek mein 2 pahiye. Guess karo: 5 se zyada pahiye ya kam?
hints: Each cycle has more than one wheel.
So will the wheels be more than the cycles?
More wheels than cycles: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = ___.
More — 10 wheels.

items.prompt_en: For 3 bags with 5 apples in each, why do we add 5 three times?
items.prompt_hi: 3 thaile, har ek mein 5 seb. Hum 5 ko teen baar kyun jodte hain?
items.answer: One 5 for each bag, and there are 3 bags
hints: How many apples in one bag?
How many bags?
We add ___ once for each of the ___ bags.
Each bag has 5, and there are 3 bags, so 5 + 5 + 5.

items.prompt_en: Plates with 2, 3, 2 rotis — or plates with 3, 3, 3 rotis. Which shows equal groups?
items.prompt_hi: 2, 3, 2 rotiyon wali plates — ya 3, 3, 3 rotiyon wali plates. Kaun barabar group dikhaata hai?
hints: Check each set: are all the numbers the same?
2, 3, 2 — is one different?
Equal groups are ___, ___, ___.
3, 3, 3 — every plate has the same number.

items.prompt_en: Bholu has 3 plates with 4 laddoos each. He says 3 + 4 = 7 laddoos. What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Bholu ke paas 3 plates hain, har ek pe 4 laddoo. Woh kehta hai 3 + 4 = 7 laddoo. Kya galat hai?
hints: Is 3 a number of laddoos or a number of plates?
Each plate gives 4 laddoos.
Bholu added the plates — it should be 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

items.prompt_en: Turn 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 into a story about chappals.
items.prompt_hi: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 ko chappalon ki kahani mein badlo.
items.answer: Any story with 4 pairs of chappals, making 8 chappals
hints: Chappals come in twos. How many 2s are there?
So how many pairs?
___ pairs of chappals make ___ chappals.
For example: 4 children left their pairs of chappals at the door — 8 chappals.

items.prompt_en: 2 cows, each has 4 legs. How many legs?
items.prompt_hi: 2 gaayein, har ek ki 4 taangein. Kitni taangein?
hints: How many legs on one cow?
Add 4 for each cow.
8 legs.

items.prompt_en: Each child eats 2 rotis. 4 children eat. How many rotis must be made?
items.prompt_hi: Har bachcha 2 roti khaata hai. 4 bachche khaate hain. Kitni rotiyaan banani padengi?
hints: How many rotis for one child?
Add 2 for each child.
8 rotis.

items.prompt_en: Teach Chintu how to find the number of wheels on 4 cycles.
items.prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao 4 cycle ke kitne pahiye hain, kaise nikaale.
items.answer: Each cycle has 2 wheels, so add 2 four times: 2, 4, 6, 8 — 8 wheels
hints: How many wheels on one cycle?
How many times should he add that?
Add ___ four times: 2, 4, ___, ___.

items.prompt_en: 3 plates, 2 bananas on each. How many bananas?
items.prompt_hi: 3 plates, har plate pe 2 kele. Kitne kele?
hints: Count bananas, not plates.
Add 2 for each plate.
6 bananas.

workedExample.problem: 3 auto-rickshaws, each has 3 wheels. How many wheels?
steps: Check the groups are equal: every auto has 3 wheels.
Count the groups: 3 autos.
Add 3 once for each auto: 3 + 3 + 3.
3 + 3 = 6, 6 + 3 = 9. There are 9 wheels.

skills.title: Counts in twos up to 20
Counts in fives up to 50
Links skip counting to equal groups ("three twos" = 2 + 2 + 2)

expectations: Counting in twos means saying every second number: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10
Counting in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20
The last number you land on is the total, the same as adding again and again
"Three twos" and 2 + 2 + 2 are the same amount

misconceptions.belief: Thinks 2 + 2 + 2 and "three twos" give different answers
signs: Recounts when the same thing is said a new way
Says "three twos" is 3 or 5

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is "three twos" the same as 2 + 2 + 2?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya "teen do" (2 ke teen group) aur 2 + 2 + 2 ek hi baat hai?

remediation.representation: The same 3 pairs of chappals labelled two ways: "three twos" and "2 + 2 + 2"
remediation.moveShape: Point to the same picture while saying both names, then count it once

misconceptions.belief: When skip counting, thinks the number of counting words said is the total (2, 4, 6 means 3 things)
signs: Says "3 chappals" after counting 2, 4, 6
Counts the skip-count words on fingers

diagnostic.prompt_en: We counted 3 pairs of chappals: "2, 4, 6". How many chappals are there?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Humne chappal ke 3 jode gine: "2, 4, 6". Kitni chappal hain?

remediation.representation: Each skip-count word lights up two chappals at once
remediation.moveShape: Ask "how many pairs?" and "how many chappals?" separately

items.prompt_en: Count in twos: 2, 4, 6, ___?
items.prompt_hi: Do-do karke gino: 2, 4, 6, ___?
hints: Each step jumps 2.
Two more than 6 is...?
6, 7, ___ — say only the second one.

items.prompt_en: Count in fives: 5, 10, 15, ___?
items.prompt_hi: Paanch-paanch karke gino: 5, 10, 15, ___?
hints: Each step jumps 5.
Five more than 15 is...?

items.prompt_en: There are 4 pairs of chappals outside the temple. Count in twos. How many chappals?
items.prompt_hi: Mandir ke bahar chappal ke 4 jode hain. Do-do karke gino. Kitni chappal?
hints: Each pair is 2. Say one number per pair.
8 chappals.

items.prompt_en: Riya and Sonu hold up both hands — that is 4 hands. Count in fives. How many fingers?
items.prompt_hi: Riya aur Sonu dono haath upar karte hain — 4 haath. Paanch-paanch karke gino. Kitni ungliyaan?
hints: Each hand has 5 fingers.
Say one number per hand: 5, 10...
20 fingers.

items.prompt_en: Count in twos: 10, 12, 14... Guess the number that comes after 18.
items.prompt_hi: Do-do karke gino: 10, 12, 14... Guess karo 18 ke baad kaun sa aayega?
hints: After 14 comes 16, then 18.
Two more than 18?

items.prompt_en: Why is counting in twos faster for counting chappals?
items.prompt_hi: Chappal ginne ke liye do-do karke ginna jaldi kyun hai?
items.answer: Chappals come in pairs, so each number counts a whole pair and we skip saying the number in between
hints: How do chappals usually come?
How many numbers do we say for each pair?
They come in ___, so one number counts ___.
Chappals come in pairs — one number per pair means fewer numbers to say.

items.prompt_en: "Three twos" and "2 + 2 + 2" — same or different?
items.prompt_hi: "Teen do" aur "2 + 2 + 2" — ek jaise ya alag?
hints: How many 2s are in "three twos"?
How many 2s are in 2 + 2 + 2?
Both are ___.
